item.title: Morning Coffee: Tragedy of the gentle Citi VP who asked a colleague to lunch. Bad news is good news for PwC partners
item.description:
Some stories have lessons for us all to learn, and some are just incomprehensible and sad things that happened to people in the banking industry. A court in London has been hearing <https://www.thetimes.com/uk/crime/article/girlfriend-cierpka-killed-banker-boyfriend-slotsaa-trial-7dmmgtlbq> about the death of Citi vice president (VP) Henrik Slotsaa , which is very much the second kind.
Slotsaa was very well liked </news/henrik-slotsaa-citi>in Citigroup's UK office; he worked on the operations </news/operations-jobs-banking> team for loan capital markets, and colleagues told us previously he was "a nice and gentle guy."
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Slotsaa was in a relationship with Joanna Cierpka, who he'd been with since 2011. The court heard that Cierpka became depressed after being made redundant from her job outside financial services, and that she feared that Slotsaa would leave her.
The case is ongoing, but the court was also told this week that Henrik shared some of his problems at home with a colleague at Citi whom he regularly met for lunch. The court heard that Cierpka found out about this friendship. The precise details of what happened after that are still coming out in court, but the prosecution's case is that Cierpka stabbed Slotsaa multiple times, and that his body was not found for around a week.
Joanna Cierpka denies murder but has pleaded guilty to manslaughter on grounds of diminished responsibility; one psychiatrist called by the prosecution has told the court the killing followed jealousy and the breakdown of the relationship, against a backdrop of Cierpka's alcohol use.
When the news of Henrik's death came out earlier this year, Citigroup told us that "We are deeply saddened by the tragic loss of our colleague. Our thoughts are with Henrik's family and friends during this difficult time." It's slightly sobering to think that there are so many people we work with and whose company we value through the working day, but have no idea what might be going on in their private lives. Be kind to one another is probably the only thing remaining to say.
Elsewhere, it is not a great time for accountants and professional services firms. Although their fortunes usually tend to wax and wane alongside the investment banking </news/what-is-an-investment-bank> industry, this year has seen a significant concentration of revenue – the aggregate figures are very much driven by a small number of sectors and a small number of big deals, and that means that they have mostly accrued to a small number of banks.
It’s been particularly difficult <https://www.ft.com/content/bb2c178f-08e8-4de2-af49-6c184217cfb3?syn-25a6b1a6=1> for PwC’s UK practice, because that is where the global firm also holds its Middle East operations, and these are also suffering from a slowdown in deals, which has come after a lot of investment went into the region. A 15% fall in MENA revenue in the 12 months to June was more than enough to offset the 2% increase in domestic business, meaning that PwC saw revenues fall 3% over the period, the first annual decline for more than twenty years.
You might think this would be reflected in partners’ pay. It wasn't. The average PwC partner got £935k ($1.25m) for the year, up 8%. This might be because PwC partners own the business. In good years, payouts can be low as partners use profits to invest in the business. In a year like the one we’ve just had, there’s much less reason to do this.
This is a theme that’s likely to be repeated across the big professional services firms as they follow PwC in reporting on the last year’s business; KPMG is already consulting <https://www.hcamag.com/asia/news/general/low-attrition-levels-at-kpmg-uk-put-roles-at-risk/589914> on compulsory redundancies in its advisory business because natural attrition isn’t moving headcount fast enough.
Meanwhile …
David Solomon says Goldman Sachs’ FICC business is going to be “a little softer, on a relative basis” in Q3. He also noted that “there are still a few weeks left in September” implying that it’s close enough that a really good last fortnight could save the quarter. Since some analysts were forecasting 11% sequential declines, things might actually be a bit better than expected. Equities trading is still “very strong”. (Reuters <https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/goldman-ceo-says-fixed-income-currencies-commodities-business-slightly-softer-q3-2026-09-16/>)
It’s perhaps a little hard to get your head round the idea that there might be unexploited alpha in a global weather phenomenon that everyone has known about for months. But Zulfiqar Ali, who started his own hedge fund ZAMS two years ago at the age of 32 after leaving Balyasny, thinks that the market is underestimating the effect of a strong El Nino this year and that with the help of accurate weather forecasts and a commodity trader’s nerve, he can boost returns. (Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-16/ex-balyasny-trader-bets-el-nino-can-turbocharge-hedge-fund-gains>)
Litigation funding is a fascinating niche of the hedge fund industry, but it’s more of a people business than anything else. Tempers are always likely to run high when an investor and a lawyer disagree about the most sensible way to deal with a settlement offer. (FT <https://www.ft.com/content/6ec74be5-9e4c-49c0-a9dc-d3a0ae324a17?syn-25a6b1a6=1>)
“You don’t want to start planning for an engine failure when you’re at 24,000 feet”. This is how wealth managers try to get across the concept of investment risk and diversification to airline pilots. (WSJ <https://www.wsj.com/personal-finance/the-volatile-finances-of-airline-pilots-americas-unpredictable-millionaires-cd403364?st=ouLULN&reflink=desktopwebshare_permalink>)
Miami has a great beach, Dubai is tax efficient, Athens has the Parthenon … but when you’re serious about attracting hedge fund talent, the location feature that they are most interested in is often “somewhere convenient for my house”. That seems to be the rationale behind Brevan Howard’s decision to open up an office in Greenwich, Connecticut. (Business Insider <https://www.businessinsider.com/brevan-howard-new-greenwich-office-talent-war-location-2027-2026-9>)
Adrian Cudrig an equity capital markets banker at Morgan Stanley is apparently driving around Sydney in a Maserati Ghibli with the license plate “ECMGUY”. All one can say is to agree with the AFR columnist; “Hell yeah, brother”. (AFR <https://www.afr.com/rear-window/firmus-ipo-banker-s-personalised-maserati-20260914-p60x5n>)

item.title: UBS may be cutting costs, but if you're a US banker who's worked for Credit Suisse it's hiring
item.description:
UBS has costs to cut. At the start of this year, it promised to extract around $1.1bn from its compensation line. </news/ubs-will-be-cutting-another-1-1bn-from-employment-costs-this-year>At the end of June, it had actually increased group-level compensation spending from $14bn in the first half of 2025 to nearly $15bn in the first half of 2026.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Amends must presumably be made. UBS declined to comment for this article, but senior insiders told us cuts are likely later this month or in October. They won't be the first this year. Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-05-29/ubs-sheds-hundreds-in-latest-job-cuts-after-credit-suisse-deal>reported in May that 'several hundred positions', mostly in support functions, had been eliminated.
While UBS is trimming, though, it's also hiring. Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-14/ubs-bolsters-us-investment-bank-with-senior-industrial-hires> <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-15/meta-touts-the-cost-saving-benefits-of-latest-in-house-ai-chips>reported on Monday that it has hired five managing directors, two vice chairmen and one executive director for its US banking business. Six of them have previously spent time at Credit Suisse.
The H1B visa database says UBS pays its managing directors salaries of at least $350k. If it likes you, it will pay even more. It will also pay bonuses, often guaranteed, for new hires. The five MDs, two chairman and ED are therefore unlikely to have come cheaply.
The new hires are:
Justin Kish, a Credit Suisse banker between 2010 and 2016, latterly at Rothschild. Joining as an MD in building products and materials.
Christian Hartenberger, a Credit Suisse banker between 2001 and 2014, latterly at BNP Paribas and very briefly at Santander. Joining as an MD focused on aerospace and defence.
Pierre Bosse, a Credit Suisse banker between 2004 and 2021, latterly at JPMorgan. Joining as an MD focused on energy and power.
Adam Reeder, a Credit Suisse banker between 2010 and 2015, latterly at Rothschild. Now vice chairman of the UBS global industrials group.
Matt Parr, a Credit Suisse banker between 2004 and 2012, latterly at PJT. Now vice chair and head of Midwest banking at UBS.
Evan Bergelt, briefly at Credit Suisse from 2017-2019. Also joining from Rothschild, to be executive director in industrials.
Jeff Vergamini from Deutsche Bank, as an MD covering industrials M&A.
Brian Willer from Deutsche Bank, as an MD covering automotive and mobility.
UBS therefore seems likely to have spent at least $5m on its new US bankers when bonuses are factored in, and probably a lot more.
The array of ex-Credit Suisse hires comes as UBS's array of ex-Barclays hires have been leaving. Richard Hardegree <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-05-08/bank-of-america-hires-ubs-tech-banker-hardegree>, for example, went to BofA in May.
UBS's US M&A business has big aspirations but still needs to meet them. It ranked 22nd for US M&A deals by fees generated </news/don-t-disparage-the-ubs-us-m-and-a-bankers-who-are-hard-at-work>in the first half of the year.
Taylor Henricks now runs UBS's US M&A business, having joined from Morgan Stanley in October 2025. He also runs UBS's technology banking business, but UBS has not ranked in the top 10 globally for technology deals since 2023. </news/highest-paid-bankers>
It's not clear who hired all the new ex-Credit Suisse people to the US team but Emre Gunalp, the US head of industrials banking at UBS also spent 20 years at Credit Suisse before transitioning to UBS in the dark days of 2023.

item.title: The new man to know at Citadel in London was once an M&A analyst at Goldman Sachs
item.description:
There is a new big man at hedge fund Citadel in London. The Financial Times <https://www.ft.com/content/41fb2ff1-fb84-4ae4-8668-59d46842dcdb?syn-25a6b1a6=1> reported last week that Drew Gillanders, the lightly-stubbled head of international equities, is leaving aged 54. Gillanders has been removed from Citadel's website; 40-year-old Nabeel Bhanji <https://www.citadel.com/who-we-are/leadership/nabeel-bhanji/>has replaced him.
We reported </news/nabeel-bhanji-citadel> upon Bhanji's arrival from Elliott Management in November 2024. Bhanji was a star at Elliott and we suggested that Citadel might have paid him £5m+. That now seems a significant understatement.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Bhanji isn't replacing Gillanders directly. Citadel hired Bhanji to lead a business called 'Strategic Equity Investments, ' which allows Citadel portfolio managers to take large positions and to hold them for a long time. Members of the SEI team are also encouraged to have a dialogue with the management and boards of portfolio companies, said the FT.
Gillanders, meanwhile, was running Citadel's long-short International Equities business in Europe and Asia. He had been doing so since June 2023 and previously worked for Point72, where he was a fan of Steve Cohen.
Gillanders exit from Citadel was precipitated by the combining of Citadel's SEI business, run by Bhanjii and Citadel's International Equities business run by Gillanders. Bhanji now overseas a business covering it all: long-short, risk arb, and SEI.
If you want an equities job at Citadel in London or Asia, Bhanji is therefore the man to know. He began his career at Goldman Sachs, where he briefly worked in M&A </news/get-a-job-in-ma> before the financial crisis, before escaping to private equity and then to Elliott.
Gillanders also began his career in M&A, but at Morgan Stanley, where he spent nearly nine years and worked under Paul Taubman. Speaking to students two years ago </news/citadel-hedge-fund-jobs-london>, Gillanders said he spent a lot of time interviewing for Citadel and looked for people who reacted well in both a draw-up and a draw-down.
Gillanders also said that Citadel lets its portfolio managers take a longer term view than other funds. Speaking on one of Citadel's own videos <https://lnkd.in/p/eU6cVh3D> he said the firm has a "social contract" with the people it hires and that it invests in them. Now he will take that investment elsewhere.
Bhanjii, meanwhile, may want to hire his own people. In December 2024, the FT <https://www.ft.com/content/4a036dae-8791-4d11-94d7-ce97759c6bf3?syn-25a6b1a6=1> said Citadel also hired Pawel Serej from Elliott to work in London; the FCA Register shows him arriving in September 2025. Sergey Pichugov also joined Citadel from Elliott's macro team in January.
The Citadel Equities Fund was up over 23% through to Aug 31st. Citadel declined to comment.

item.title: RBC’s head of global equity sales left for a curious French stockbroker
item.description:
Everyone in finance is climbing a ladder. Some people leave their company for a bigger one, with a bigger ladder; some people leave for a similar sized one offering them a step up. Sometimes, people leave for a much smaller one offering them a very big step up.
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/login?_gl=1*ut8n6u*_gcl_au*MTg4MDY2NTExNi4xNzYxNTU3NDIz*_ga*ODczNzI2NTA0LjE3NTM2OTk2ODI.*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3NjM2NDM0MDYkbzI1NiRnMSR0MTc2MzY0MzQzOSRqMjckbDAkaDMyMjc4OTUzMw..>✍️
Pamela Addoh joined ODDO BHF in London last month to lead its global market sales team. Addoh left for Oddo from RBC Capital Markets, where she was head of both the global equity and us equity sales teams. She was at Deutsche Bank before that.
ODDO BHF is an odd place to go. Founded in the 60s by a Marseille-based stockbroker, it bought the German bank BHF back in 2016 and merged with it. ODDO BHF brought on Addoh specifically to grow its transatlantic business.
ODDO BHF has a number of businesses under its umbrella; asset and wealth management, investment banking (including equities, fixed income, and commodities) as well as general corporate banking and research. Its cash equity sales team specifically is part of a curious swap that it did with Natixis back in 2017 </news/2020/02/natixis-investment-bank-boutiques>, in which it acquired that team – as well as the trading team – from Natixis, in exchange for its equity capital markets </news/capital-markets-jobs-ecm-and-dcm> team. The things we do for MIFID.

item.title: Evercore's London pay shot up. But only for a select group
item.description:
Boutique investment banks </news/boutique-investment-banks> like Evercore are well known for their compensation. But average compensation of $1m or however much includes wide swaths of high-earners and low-earners (relatively low, at least). Full-year 2025 accounts published today for Evercore’s London-based subsidiaries – namely, Evercore Partners International LLP and Evercore Group Services Limited – could offer a useful breakdown.
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/login?_gl=1*ut8n6u*_gcl_au*MTg4MDY2NTExNi4xNzYxNTU3NDIz*_ga*ODczNzI2NTA0LjE3NTM2OTk2ODI.*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3NjM2NDM0MDYkbzI1NiRnMSR0MTc2MzY0MzQzOSRqMjckbDAkaDMyMjc4OTUzMw..>✍️
The topline figures were very good. Evercore made £528m ($711m) in the UK in 2025, up significantly from £379m ($511m) it made in 2024. Profit went up even more dramatically, from £180m ($242m) in 2024 to £305m ($411m) in 2025.
Pay for the firm’s members – UK legal jargon for partners in a partnership – was up accordingly, from £1.3m ($1.7m) per head in 2024 to £2.0m ($2.7m) per head. That was both due to an increase in profit and a decrease in members. In a boutique investment bank, most of its “members” are dealmakers, who are senior managing directors </news/banks-weird-hierarchies-analysts-associates-vps-mds>, and other parts of the Evercore business such as its French subsidiary. The largest single payout for an Evercore member was £16m ($22m), which might have gone to a corporate member
Pay was not up for everyone, however. Regular pay for staff was £114k in 2025, flat on the £114k that Evercore paid its people in 2024. That was partly because Evercore hired a big chunk of people in London – headcount went up from 386 in 2024 to 428 in 2025, driven by an increase in both “professional staff” and “administrative staff”.
That might change in 2026 Evercore had a great 2025 globally </news/evercore-q4-2025>, and 2026 is shaping up to be just as good; H1 revenue in 2026 </news/evercore-q2-2026> was up 56% on 2025, although hiring slowed down substantially. That might have something to do with the bank’s partnership with OpenAI, and its contribution to developing <https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-financial-services/> “ChatGPT for financial services”. Hiring might slow down; revenues should not.

item.title: Nomura's macro people are still joining hedge funds. So are its operations types
item.description:
Once, we said </news/2022/05/nomura-fx-jobs>that Nomura traders are particularly suited to work in hedge funds </news/how-to-get-a-hedge-fund-job>. This is because they are particularly used to taking proprietary risk. Accordingly, many leave for this destination. </news/nomura-paid-its-bonuses-and-now-some-traders-are-leaving>
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
This year, Nomura's macro business appears to have lost a lot of macro traders, particularly in Singapore </news/another-asian-rates-guy-has-exited-nomura>where it has coincidentally also hired a lot of traders from ANZ.
Now, macro traders are also leaving Nomura's other offices. Nomura isn't commenting, but sources say that Lynn Xie, a director-level US dollar options trader in New York has vanished. So has Lim Jia Cong, an MD on the same desk. The destination of both is unclear.
In London, Lorenzo Chiesa, a junior on the FX options desk has also left. He has joined Citadel to trade FX vol, relative value and macro. Sam Green, an executive director on the London rates options desk, also left in August according to the FCA register.
Macro insiders at Nomura say the departures reflect their popularity with hedge funds. One suggested that Citadel likes to hire them. Maja Vengust and Radwan El Chab also left Nomura's London macro business for Citadel last year.
It's not just macro traders. In an internal memo sent last week, Nomura explained that Aleem Jivraj, its global markets COO, has been replaced with Varun Luthra, a risk manager who has worked for Nomura for nearly 20 years. Jivraj has gone to Balyasny. </news/balyasny-hedge-fund>

item.title: Morning Coffee: How to get a senior banker to like you, a technique. JPMorgan gives investment bankers cause for cheer
item.description:
More or less everything about recruiting students <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-15/job-market-for-bankers-on-wall-street-has-never-been-harder-to-crack?cmpid=091526_morningamer&utm_campaign=morningamer&utm_medium=email&utm_source=newsletter&utm_term=260915&utm_content=8919> into investment banking </news/what-is-an-investment-bank> internships </news/internship-investment-bank> is awful, for everyone involved. Human resources departments get a pile of applications </news/how-many-intern-applications>which is literally a hundred times the number of places available. University careers departments have to turn themselves into temporary therapists, advising elite young people how to cope with rejection when they’ve never experienced it before.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
And the students are put through the slog of sending dozens of individualised applications </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-banking> explaining what they think is unique about every bank on the Street, putting endless time into preparation and extracurriculars, in order to prepare for an interview </news/70-top-banking-interview-questions-and-how-to-answer-them>process that’s often as short as 2.5 hours. As one of them says, “It’s a pretty big mismatch”. Needless to say, introducing AI </news/agentic-ai-for-banking-jobs> into the process has made things considerably worse.
About the only people who have any prospect of enjoyment at all are bankers with a bit of spare time in September, who might get a subsidised trip to their alma mater for an “information session”, allowing them to show off and consume cheap alcohol. But even this isn’t risk free. The cost of being a big figure on campus for one evening is that later in the year, you will suddenly get dozens of connection requests and social media messages, with keen students who “happen to be in town” and would like to “catch up for a coffee” and perhaps “pick your brains”.
It’s hard to say no to such an invitation; quite apart from anything, you never know if you might accidentally be offending a young relative of someone important. So bankers often find themselves spending time during the months from April to June being taken away from their desks to sip flat whites as prominent members of university finance societies try to form a bond with them.
The strategy adopted by one undergraduate at Western Ontario university is worth reproducing, as it sounds absolutely terrifying. According to Bloomberg, he says “Keep digging for common ground … even if the banker on the other end of the conversation sounds completely uninterested …I will not move on until the five minutes are done … You just keep circling, circling in until you can build that connection.”
In a normal banking interview, this would be absolute career death. Bankers are famous for using the “airport test” to make hiring decisions – since it will certainly happen at some point, is this a person that I could bear to be stuck with for six hours at an airport during a flight delay?
But, of course, the thing about interns is that you probably won’t get the ones that you spoke to, and even if you end up working with them long term they will hopefully have done a bit of growing up in the meantime. So the super-intense approach is likely to be less off-putting than it sounds.
Intern recruitment is never going to be easy. You are trying to identify the people who will make good investment bankers, at an age when they don’t know who they are, and when all they really know about the industry is that’s it’s prestigious and has a structured process full of tests they can pass. But it feels like there has to be a better way than this.
Elsewhere, it seems that thanks to Doug Petno of JP Morgan <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-15/jpmorgan-sees-third-quarter-investment-banking-trading-gains>, the Barclays Global Financial Services Conference isn’t going to end on a gloomy note. Yesterday, we noted </news/bank-of-america-q3> that Brian Moynihan of Bank of America had been guiding expectations downward for investment banking revenue, but that this might reflect company-specific issues (particularly, a sectoral profile of clients which wasn’t heavily weighted to tech) rather than general industry malaise.
But Petno says JPM is still expecting both trading revenue and fee income to be up “by a percentage in the mid to high teens”. This would be against a fairly tough base for comparison, and would certainly point to a very strong revenue year.
It isn’t clear quite why there’s such a difference. JPM does have a top rated tech team </news/highest-paid-bankers>, which has traded the number one spot back and forth with Goldman Sachs over the last few years. But it was in roughly the same bookrunner position as BoA in the syndicate for SpaceX, and neither bank is slated to lead OpenAI or Anthropic, the other two megadeals for H2. Maybe it’s just a matter of small wins and calendar effects, or maybe some bankers are just naturally more optimistic than others.
Meanwhile …
“Am I in favour of blocking someone from entering the nightclub? The answer is no”. That was the official line from the Socialist Party in France about whether Evercore banker Matthieu Pigasse would be allowed to run in their Presidential primary. But things seem to have happened, and it appears that the punk rock </news/2021/09/bankers-who-were-punks> superstar of sovereign restructuring </news/matthieu-pigasse> will remain outside the velvet rope this time. (Le Monde <%22Am%20I%20in%20favor%20of%20blocking%20someone%20from%20entering%20the%20nightclub?%20The%20answer%20is%20no,>)
Private equity </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-private-equity> firms seem to be moving beyond using ChatGPT to churn out pitchbooks, and are now specifically acquiring companies where they think that implementing AI solutions can help them make return targets. (FT <https://www.ft.com/content/a43e9050-f646-4d24-b650-b75ef589985c?syn-25a6b1a6=1>)
Goldman Sachs Private Wealth Management has been running “NextGS Investment Intensive”, a sort of boot camp for nepos, in which younger members of very rich families are taught how to invest their money when they inherit it. There are also modules on buying luxury watches and handbags. (NY Post <https://nypost.com/2026/09/14/business/inside-goldmans-bootcamp-for-ultra-rich-gen-z-heirs-how-to-read-the-news-buy-luxury-watches-and-invest-in-sports-teams/>)
As former BoA star Mike Lyons </news/jpmorgan-jane-street> has departed to run Truist, another high-flying banker has been called in to replace him at fintech infrastructure provider Fiserv. Takis Georgakopoulos was once seen as a long shot for the top job at JP Morgan (FT <https://www.ft.com/content/43729997-e516-45a9-893b-de7bd729bc2f?syn-25a6b1a6=1>)
Former hedge fund </news/how-to-get-a-hedge-fund-job> manager Derek Kaufman is taking the “get it done” approach which served him well at Citadel and JP Morgan and applying it to the politics of building permit reform. (Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-14/what-is-the-abundance-movement-derek-kaufman-is-putting-it-into-practice?cmpid=moneynl&utm_campaign=moneynl&utm_medium=email&utm_source=newsletter&utm_term=260915&utm_content=8900>)
If you ever have to use an ejector seat in a military aircraft, the company which makes the seats will give you a free tie and enroll you in what must be one of the world’s most exclusive clubs. (WSJ <https://www.wsj.com/lifestyle/careers/eject-tie-club-military-jet-collins-martin-baker-4c8496ab?mod=hp_featst_pos5>)

item.title: Jane Street's UK pay: $1.9m per head, $55m if you're a partner
item.description:
Jane Street </news/how-to-get-a-job-at-jane-street> pays a lot of money. In 2025, it paid its global team an average of $2.7m. </news/jane-street-pay-2026>Compensation in its London office is similarly impressive.
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/login?_gl=1*ut8n6u*_gcl_au*MTg4MDY2NTExNi4xNzYxNTU3NDIz*_ga*ODczNzI2NTA0LjE3NTM2OTk2ODI.*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3NjM2NDM0MDYkbzI1NiRnMSR0MTc2MzY0MzQzOSRqMjckbDAkaDMyMjc4OTUzMw..>✍️
The electronic trading firm' </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-an-electronic-trading-firm>s UK entity, 'Jane Street UK Partnership,' filed accounts with Companies House this week. They showed that Jane Street had increased its UK headcount by over 100, growing to a total of 790 employees. At the same time, spending on 'salaries, allowances and benefits in kind' almost doubled to a total of $1.48bn. Average pay per head, therefore, was $1.88bn.
The entity also recorded profits of $1.86bn to be shared among its eight LLP members, of which two were corporate entities. The highest paid member recieved $1.54bn so, if we assume that was paid to one of the entities, the remaining partners received an average of $55.6m.
Jane Street welcomed multiple new members (partners) into its UK partnership last year. Slawomir Rzeszotko, Timothy Hennock and Maanit Desai were all appointed on January 1st 2025. FINRA's BrokerCheck tool says Hennock has worked for Jane Street since 2013 and has worked across New York, Hong Kong and London; he has been based in the UK since 2023. It also says that Desai has worked at Jane Street since 2008, and has been based in London since 2015. Both members report no prior experience via FINRA and thus appear to have once been graduate hires. </news/pay-for-electronic-trading-graduates-is-soaring-1m-at-hrt-850k-at-jane-street>Rzeszotko, who has worked in ETF business development for the firm since 2014, was an external hire. He joined from Vanguard, where he was head of the investment products specialist team.
Pre-existing members include Ian Shea, Jane Street's Europe head of fixed income trading, and John Mackenzie, Jane Street's Europe head of legal and compliance. David House, who held the title of head of trading systems in a previous Jane Street entity, is a partner too.
Jane Street has big plans for London. Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-04-28/jane-street-set-to-double-footprint-in-london-office-move> reported in April that the firm is in talks to move into a new 450,000 square foot office, almost double the size of its current location.

item.title: Deutsche Bank's US fixed income business is attracting persons from Goldman Sachs
item.description:
Deutsche Bank wants to increase its presence in US fixed income trading. </news/deutsche-bank-s-investor-day>Goldman Sachs has a strong presence in US fixed income trading. Deutsche Bank is hiring people from Goldman Sachs, sometimes circuitously.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Deutsche has, for example, hired Puneet Agarwal, who spent 14 years at Goldman working a hybrid role involving the investment bank, engineering and macro strategy. Agarwal left his job as a Goldman MD in June 2022, and has spent the past four years running a fintech. <https://www.stimson.org/ppl/puneet-agarwal/>Now he's back, and he is Deutsche Bank's US head of macro structuring.
Deutsche has also made a hire directly from Goldman. The German bank poached Luke Merrill, a vice president on Goldman's CLO trading desk for a role in US CLO trading. Merrill, who is understood to be aged only 28, will be reporting to Matthew Matson. Matson is a Deutsche Bank MD and head of leveraged loan trading.
Matson once worked for Mizuho.
Deutsche Bank declined to comment.

item.title: Pay for electronic trading graduates is soaring: $1m at HRT, $850k at Jane Street
item.description:
Very few people are able to make it to the promised land of electronic trading. </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-an-electronic-trading-firm> Graduates that do so are able to earn staggering amounts of money, </news/hudson-river-trading-pay> but if you're hired by Hudson River Trading, you'll make more money than the rest.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
We've spoken to multiple insiders in the electronic trading space to understand what kind of compensation packages were offered to 2026 summer interns </news/electronic-trading-summer-internship-pay> returning full-time in 2027. Multiple sources have attested that Hudson River Trading </news/hudson-river-trading-pay-uk-high-frequency-trading> (HRT) is the most generous of the major trading firms, offering a first-year compensation package of $1m, although it did not respond to a request for comment to confirm this. Anonymous sources suggest that the largest component of the package is a sign-on bonus, which can reach up to $400k. This is supposedly the "scraps"; </news/hudson-river-trading-pay> senior people at the firm can earn upwards of $100m per year.
Last year, HRT appeared to pay most new graduates up to $700k. In a recent podcast <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cmnXNkby2SE>, ex-HRT algo developer Su Min Lee said that first-year compensation offers for new joiners were "in the $550k to $700k range." Lee said that, when she joined the firm in 2021, her compensation was around $375k, but she said this was on the lower end and that returning interns (which she was not) earned more. Insiders say that $1m has been achievable for top interns in the past.
At Hudson River Trading, multiple software engineers on Levels.fyi <https://www.levels.fyi/en-gb/companies/hudson-river-trading/salaries/software-engineer?country=254> with zero years of experience also reported total compensation of over $700k last year; HRT insiders say that compensation for tech and algo development is broadly similar at entry level but traders can differentiate themselves more as they become more senior.
Opinions on first-year compensation at Jane Street </news/this-is-what-it-takes-to-get-a-64k-jane-street-internship>were mixed but sources within electronic trading firms suggest that $850k packages for 2027 graduates are the most common. It was suggested that the firm could offer $1m packages too. Jane Street declined to comment. Figures for Citadel Securities </news/2022/10/how-to-get-a-job-at-citadel> were not as readily available, but we understand it is highly competitive. Both firms paid their total headcount an average of over $2m per head last year. </news/citadel-securities-pay-2m>
We understand that Jump Trading </news/jump-trading-uk-pay> made offers in excess of $900k to some candidates for 2027 graduate roles, but the average offer sat closer to $750k. We understand also that Susquehanna </news/a-high-frequency-trading-firm-just-hired-bjarne-stroustrup-creator-of-c> offered within a range of $600k to $800k+. Both firms declined to comment.
Word on pay at the other trading firms was more sparse. Anonymous sources suggest Optiver </news/optiver-ai-lab>will pay 2027 graduates $700k and that IMC Trading </news/electronic-trading-firm-imc-has-quadrupled-headcount-in-london-since-2024>, which increased compensation to $425k last year, </news/a-high-frequency-trading-firm-is-offering-its-interns-425k-to-come-back-as-open-ai-looms> increased pay again to $500k. Sources close to New York-based Jane Street spinout Five Rings </news/a-trading-firm-spun-out-of-jane-street-pays-673k-in-london-and-is-hiring> say it pays graduates $700k. These firms did not respond to a request for comment.
Why such a drastic increase in pay? A lot has changed for electronic trading firms in the past few years, not least their skyrocketing revenues. In 2025, Jane Street generated a record $39.6bn in net trading revenues, HRT made $12.3bn and Citadel Securities made $12.2bn. It seems like things have been even better this year; Jane Street, despite losing ~$15bn during the Situational Awareness crash, had made over $40bn in trading revenues as of August. <https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/jane-street-took-15-billion-hit-july-tied-situational-awareness-sources-say-2026-08-14/>
You could also argue that it is an ongoing response from these firms to prevent AI labs like Anthropic from taking their top talent. </news/openai-culture> The particularly large signing bonuses might be seen as a more immediate alternative to receiving stock pay that could take years to pay out, especially now that OpenAI has delayed its IPO <https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/12/openai-delays-ipo-sam-altman-ai-safety-concerns>over AI safety fears. An opening for a 2027 graduate engineering role at OpenAI offers just $185k in salary alongside its equity package.

item.title: Goldman Sachs might be warming up for some more job cuts soon
item.description:
It's September, and if you work for Goldman Sachs </news/how-to-get-a-job-goldman-sachs>, this often means job cuts. Historically, Goldman Sachs has pruned underperformers in September. Sources at the firm tell us this may be about to occur again.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Goldman Sachs is declining to comment on these suggestions. The firm cut 3-4% of its people in September 2024 </news/goldman-sachs-job-cuts>and made cuts around September in both 2022 and 2023. <https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/goldman-sachs-plans-fresh-round-job-cuts-underperformers-ft-2023-09-08/>In 2024, it cut between 1,300 and 1,800 people <https://www.wsj.com/finance/banking/goldman-sachs-to-lay-off-over-1-300-workers-f1d92b88?st=zl9tg6onaie8vct&reflink=article_copyURL_share>at this time of year.
Goldman's September job cuts usually occur as part of its dryly named "strategic resource assessment" (SRA). First it appraises people. Then it identifies low performers who only "partially meet" expectations. Then it sends some of them on their way.
This year, Goldman has been doing things a bit differently. Business Insider <https://www.businessinsider.com/goldman-sachs-layoffs-cuts-underperformers-sra-spring-summer-2026-3> reported in March that Goldman would be making rolling layoffs throughout the year instead of one big round of cuts in September. However, it also said the more traditional September round could still occur.
Goldman Sachs may not necessarily need to cut costs, having massaged its compensation ratio (costs as a percentage of revenues) to the lowest level in a decade </news/goldman-pay-2026>during the first half of 2026. However, Goldman Sachs may want to cut costs because it, too </news/bank-of-america-is-only-replacing-75-of-employees-who-leave>, is keen on AI </news/goldman-sachs-assembly-line>and it has six workstreams for engineering processes "from the ground up." </news/hsbc-ai-job-cuts>
Goldman Sachs' CEO David Solomon </news/david-solomon-goldman-sachs> is due to talk </news/bank-of-america-q3>at the Barclays Global Financial Services Conference tomorrow. More may become apparent then.

item.title: Pay for Vitol's London commodities traders fell by over £1m per head
item.description:
Commodities traders </news/commodities-trading-houses> can be some of the most well paid people in the world when markets get volatile, but they can also suffer more harshly than most. At oil trading </news/how-do-you-get-a-job-in-sales-and-trading-in-a-bank>specialist Vitol, profits halved in 2025, and compensation for its UK staff dropped massively alongside it.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
'Vitol Broking Limited' released accounts for 2025 through the UK's Companies House this week. The firm reported a slight increase in headcount from 175 in 2024 to 179, but it also stated that spending on 'employee remuneration' fell by almost £100m. Compensation per head was a staggering £2.7m in 2024, but it slumped to £1.55m last year. It's still eye watering... just a bit less so.
Pre tax profits for the entity fell by much more than remuneration; it made £200m in 2024 but just £90m in 2025. The firm is a service provider to Vitol's global trading entity, and reports income as 'rendering of services,' rather than trading revenues, so it's not clear exactly how the London team performed.
The compensation was likely distributed evenly at the most senior level. Vitol is jointly owned by roughly 600 of its global employees, and no one person is allowed to own more than 5% of the firm's total value. From 2022 to 2024, it paid those shareholders a total of $20bn. </news/vitol-pay#:~:text=other%20financial%20firms%20might%20boast%20about%20the%20number%20of%20millionaires%20they%E2%80%99ve%20created%2C%20but%20Vitol%20has%20distributed%20over%20%2420%20billion%20to%20its%20600%20top%20employee%2Dshareholders%20in%20the%20last%20three%20years.>
Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-24/vitol-paid-out-5-9-billion-to-traders-as-profit-halved-in-2025?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=260724&utm_campaign=author_22490032> reported in July that Vitol's global profits in 2025 had more than halved to $4.2bn. Despite this, it said that the firm spent $5.9bn on share buybacks for its owners in 2025. It's not clear whether those buybacks, or dividends for stock owners, were reported under remuneration in its UK entity. Vitol declined to comment.

item.title: Financial services hiring in the UK has never been so average
item.description:
Working in financial services in London can sometimes inspire some daydreaming. How good things were in the past, how good things are elsewhere. But the truth might be that we are in some of the most normal times in London’s financial history.
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/login?_gl=1*ut8n6u*_gcl_au*MTg4MDY2NTExNi4xNzYxNTU3NDIz*_ga*ODczNzI2NTA0LjE3NTM2OTk2ODI.*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3NjM2NDM0MDYkbzI1NiRnMSR0MTc2MzY0MzQzOSRqMjckbDAkaDMyMjc4OTUzMw..>✍️
Data from the Office for National Statistics <https://www.ons.gov.uk/employmentandlabourmarket/peoplenotinwork/unemployment/datasets/vacanciesbyindustryvacs02/current> (ONS), released today, showed that there were 30,000 national vacancies in the financial services sector, on average, in the June-August period. That was pretty much the same as the May-July period, according to the ONS.
“Pretty much the same” ought to be the rallying cry of the UK’s financial services industry. Since 2001, the ONS’ data shows that there were 33k vacancies per month, on average, across the period. Since 2019, including both the pandemic and the post-lockdown boom, the average has been around 35k.
The data suggests that the UK’s finance sector has spun its wheels for two and a half decades. Things are different in the USA; over there, the Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS) found that vacancies can grow.
At the start of 2001, JOLTS found that the US had around 240k postings in the finance & insurance industry. In July 2026, JOLTS found 300k openings.
For the table below, the ONS's headline vacancy figures are three-month averages rather than single-month counts. Each figure below covers the three months ending in the month shown, so "June 2021" is the average of April, May and June 2021. The chart is therefore a three-month rolling average of seasonally adjusted vacancies in the finance and insurance sector.
What's wrong with UK financial services jobs? Brexit might have something to do with it. So too might the lackluster British economy and banks' growing tendency to swap AI deployment for new hires. </news/bank-of-america-is-only-replacing-75-of-employees-who-leave>Equally, though, maybe there's nothing with British banking jobs. This is normal. It's just the boom period after the pandemic that was an aberration.

item.title: Tower Research hired an ex-equities portfolio manager to manage its risk
item.description:
A lot of people want to work in an electronic trading firm </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-an-electronic-trading-firm>. Many of them are willing to work in a non-investment role to do so, but it's a rarer case for someone with a history in the front office </news/front-office-middle-office-back-office-banking>to join the middle. Pierre Danilowiez, formerly of SocGen, has done just that to work for Tower Research.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Danilowiez joined the firm's Amsterdam office as a senior risk manager. He was most recently head of investments for Arbra, a multi-family office </news/family-office-jobs>. His LinkedIn states that the role involved asset allocation for the firm's various investment teams, and the development of the firm's risk framework, which would lend itself well to a pure risk role. His role also involved "directly managing $100M+ multi-asset portfolios," which seems much more front-office oriented.
Before that, he was a trader for 15 years. He spent five years as a portfolio manager at asset manager Key Capital Partners, where he claims to have managed a €30m AUM strategy in equities. He also spent a decade at SocGen, where he was a VP in equity derivatives trading.
Danilowiez is a Grande École </news/grande-ecole-electronic-trading>mathematics and engineering graduate. French-educated equity derivatives specialists are highly sought after right now </news/french-equity-derivative-traders-are-more-popular-then-ever-not-just-with-banks>; In London, Optiver hired Barclays MD Arnaud Heckenroth as head of exotics business development, suggesting that there's further room for algo firms to expand in the already competitive world of equity derivatives.
Tower seems to prefer hiring support staff to traders right now. In 2025 accounts for its UK entity filed with Companies House this week, the firm revealed that headcount in its 'trading' unit fell by 18 while headcount in 'support/management' rose by seven. Tower did not respond to a request for comment on whether it made any cuts, or whether any staff were reassigned from a trading role into support.

item.title: Bank of America is only replacing 75% of employees who leave, but doubling the budget for AI
item.description:
It's been a while now, but Bank of America is still at it. Instead of firing people (although this sometimes occurs </news/the-bank-of-america-charts-explaining-why-it-s-resorted-to-job-cuts>), it waits for people to leave and it doesn't always replace them.
BofA CEO Brian Moynihan </news/brian-moynihan-bank-of-america> explained how this works in his market-moving conference speech </news/bank-of-america-q3> yesterday. BofA now employs around 210,000 people, down from around 213,000 people at the start of the year, said Brian.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
The bank has cut headcount by 3,000 people by only replacing around 75% of people who leave.
Brian said BofA has an employee attrition rate ranging from 8% to 8.5%. Based on current headcount, the implication is that around 1,400 people leave each month, at least.
Brian understated this and said that 1,300 people leave the bank each month. When they do, he said BofA only replaces 1,000 of them. The other 300 jobs must be 'owned' he said. More prosaically, they must be done by existing staff.
Fortunately, AI is around to help with this. "In the end of day, our teammates have got to use AI to make our company better and make our clients a better experience," declared Moynihan. BofA now has "150 use cases implemented" and is deploying AI into "more work," he said too. This work includes audit, legal and other areas. And BofA's 18,000 coders have "saved" 10-15%, which is being redeployed.
Next year, Moynihan said BofA plans to double its "expense budget" for AI. It is not spending wildly, though. "Each idea is costed out to the nth degree to say, I spend X, I get back Y and here's the payback and et cetera," he explained.
While AI enables more work to be done by fewer people, it seems that BofA's employees are still clinging to their jobs. Before the pandemic, the attrition rate at the bank ran at 12%+. </news/the-bank-of-america-charts-explaining-why-it-s-resorted-to-job-cuts>Since the pandemic it's been down to 8%. This low attrition rate made it necessary for BofA to actually cut jobs two years ago. If more people could be encouraged to quit, it would make ongoing cost-cutting easier. Unfortunately, people seem to recognise that AI might make it harder for them to find jobs elsewhere.

item.title: Ex-Deutsche Bank trader with a big new job is out after a year
item.description:
Vikram Dadlani spent a long time at Deutsche Bank. He has spent less time at Mizuho.
Dadlani, who was once Deutsche Bank's head of European investment grade trading, left Deutsche Bank after 15 years in December 2024. He joined Mizuho in September 2025
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Dadlani had a bigger job at Mizuho. There, he was head of all EMEA credit trading.
Now he has left again. The reason for his exit is unclear. Dadlani didn't respond to a request to comment for this article. Mizuho declined to comment. Maybe he is having a rest before something else.
Mizuho's credit trading team has been through some big changes. </news/mizuho-traders-leaving>Asif Godall, the former head of global markets in EMEA departed in May after what he described as "seven wonderful years" to "explore new opportunities and challenges" which he has yet to detail upon LinkedIn. Co-heads of credit trading Hardeep Bariana and Aristo Vounakis </news/mizuho-s-head-of-credit-trading-had-a-nice-long-rest-and-then-suddenly-disappeared> left in March. At least four other credit traders left too.
Maybe Mizuho needs some new ones? It's not clear who will replace Dadlani. It's thought he was hired by Godall to replace Bariana and Vounakis. Maybe they could both come back?
Alternatively, it's suggested that the credit business might now report to Steven Johnston, Mizuho's head of rates.

item.title: Morning Coffee: Bank of America's big downer. The senior woman who left Citi with no job to go to
item.description:
In case you didn't know it, the Barclays Global Financial Services Conference is on. Speaking at this conference are all kinds of CEOs of large global banks.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Yesterday's speakers included Gonzalo Luchetti, the shiny new CFO of Citigroup and Brian Moynihan </news/brian-moynihan-bank-of-america>, the deeply embedded CEO of Bank of America. Luchetti said <https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/14/bank-of-america-bac-q3-investment-banking-fees.html>things like “September is a key month. These few weeks are very meaningful,” and that severance will be increased between now and the end of the year, meaning more job cuts.
Brian, though, made some more startling declarations. He said the third quarter isn't going as great as the first and second quarters, prompting a 6% in Bank of America's share price at one point yesterday. Investment banking </news/what-is-an-investment-bank> fees across the market are down by 10% in the third quarter according to Dealogic, said Brian. BofA's fees may be slightly more disappointing still: $1.6-$1.8bn are expected; Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-14/bofa-ceo-sees-trading-revenue-relatively-flat-in-third-quarter?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=260914&utm_campaign=author_19908303>notes analysts were expecting $2bn.
Nor will the markets business pick up the slack. Although Brian Q3 will "be one of the better third quarters we ever had" for sales and trading, he also said that things are slowing. Fixed income revenues are down and erratic. Equities revenues are up, but up by less than before because Asian prime broking isn't what it was now that "people pulled the risk back."
Moynihan seemed unperturbed by all of this. "We feel the underlying economy's good and the business is good," he reflected. The 6% decline in BofA's share price suggested his ebullience wasn't assimilated elsewhere.
The question now is whether other banks will suffer similarly. Moynihan said BofA's bankers may have underperformed because they're not well positioned in sectors with a lot of activity (TMT) </news/highest-paid-bankers>. The hope is that BofA is an outlier. Luchetti said Citi's bankers and traders are heading for low and mid single digit revenue growth respectively. Goldman </news/how-to-get-a-job-goldman-sachs>CEO David Solomon </news/david-solomon-goldman-sachs>speaks tomorrow. In the meantime, Brian sparked a low single digit decline in the shares of Goldman, Morgan Stanley and Citi, too, none of which bodes well for jobs </news/citi-job-cuts-2026-new-york> or bonuses.
Separately, Financial News <https://www.fnlondon.com/articles/deutsche-banks-investment-bank-co-head-on-leadership-competition-and-women-in-dealmaking-010a5734?mod=topic_news> spoke to Alison Harding Jones, who is co-head of Deutsche Bank's investment bank, but who previously ran EMEA M&A </news/alison-harding-jones-deutsche-bank>at Citi before leaving in March 2023.
Jones, who is also known for her chickens, </news/2022/03/work-from-home-citi>said she left Citi and took 10 months off. This "gave me the space to make a considered decision with a clearer perspective," she declared. "That time was invaluable.”
Having this perspective was important, said Harding Jones. Those 10 months allowed her to choose Deutsche Bank, where the subsequent retirement of Mark Fedorcik </news/mark-fedorcik-deutsche-bank> fortuitously allowed her to take his job. Under her management, Deutsche Bank is hiring. It wants a top five position in Europe and Asia and is adding 60 bankers globally. "The UK is a critical market where we see significant opportunity," she declared, implying more bankers will be hired in London especially.
Meanwhile...
Dan Dees, co-head of global banking and markets, said financial sponsors still aren't back in the market. "While activity in that patch is up year over year, it’s up much less than the broader market." (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/newsletters/2026-09-14/goldman-s-dan-dees-on-ai-s-broad-blast-radius>
Hedge fund Elliott paid its staff an average of almost £1 million each last year. (The Times) <https://www.thetimes.com/business/companies-markets/article/elliott-hedge-funds-british-arm-pay-6s6rwvzzf>
Entry-level tech job postings have plummeted 49 percent in New York City since 2022. (NYCFuture) <. https://nycfuture.org/research/nyc-entry-level-tech-pathways-in-the-age-of-ai>
Capping bankers' bonuses is a dangerous thing. “The bonus cap can backfire: projects with a high probability of failure can become attractive...The higher fixed pay offers the manager better insurance against failure, while the bonus, even if capped, still offers some reward in case of success.” (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-14/europe-s-banker-bonus-caps-can-backfire-bis-researchers-say?taid=6aa80f7e67ebaf0001ae9c80&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_content=business&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter>
Crispin Odey has a sausage named after him and is known for his prodigious appetite. At one midweek meal with a journalist, he paired steak and kidney pudding and mash with a “side order” of a loin of beef and two bottles of wine. (Telegraph) <https://www.telegraph.co.uk/business/2026/09/14/billionaire-brexiteer-crispin-odeys-fall-from-grace/>
Crispin Odey wanted to overturn his lifetime ban but judges in an upper tribunal yesterday found that he had, "a warped set of values based on a strong sense of entitlement” and was “motivated by his own self-interest and self-preservation so as to avoid accountability.” (Financial Times) <https://www.ft.com/content/bd8a8a3f-220c-4f52-9a54-1eca0a4e0423?syn-25a6b1a6=1>

item.title: Does Hudson River Trading pay its best people $100m+?
item.description:
There are banks and then there are electronic trading firms. </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-an-electronic-trading-firm> There are electronic trading firms, and then there is Hudson River Trading (HRT). While Citadel Securities </news/citadel-securities-pay-2m> and Jane Street </news/jane-street-pay-2026>pay very, very well, there are whispers that HRT maybe pays even better. But only if it really likes you.
HRT didn't respond to a request to comment for this article, but last week's Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2026-09-10/how-jason-carroll-built-hudson-river-trading-and-a-27-billion-fortune>article on the firm suggested there might actually be pay downsides to working there. Like Jane Street, </news/jane-street-is-a-bit-communist-in-the-way-it-pays-traders> Bloomberg said HRT is a caring-sharing sort of place, and that the emphasis is on collaboration and sharing trading strategies. This makes it harder to achieve truly "spectacular" bonuses on an individual basis, said Bloomberg.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
This may be so for most people at HRT. Average pay in London can be a handsome £940k, </news/hudson-river-trading-pay-uk-high-frequency-trading> which is huge but not $100m. Newer joiners may be more likely to receive this high baseline. HRT is expanding fast. It has added at least 200 people so far this year, an increase of 20%. Many new hires are recent graduates. But multiple sources tell us that some senior people at the firm are - or at least were historically - paid Millennium-like money. </news/how-to-get-a-job-at-hedge-fund-millennium>
"Fresh out of university, you'll get the scraps," says one US headhunter who works with the firm. "It will still be a lot of money by most metrics, but nothing compared to what the top people at HRT are getting."
At the top end, he claims there people at HRT on $100m+. Multiple sources inside and outside the firm in headhunting firms confirmed this. Some told us that when HRT was founded in 2002, some non-founder employees got percentage deals that could be as high as 15% of profits. These deals are thought to have been reined-in and reduced as HRT revenues and profits have risen stratospherically. But sources say HRT will still cut lower percentage deals for the people it really wants to hire.
"They are collaborative, but they are also capitalists," says one headhunter. "If they don't pay their earners, Citadel Securities will." The recipe for earning the biggest money is tried and tested: massive PnL means massive pay.
To the extent that these deals exist, it's not clear who gets them. Insiders stress that HRT has a culture of humility and being credit shy, which would seem at odds with star payouts. Bloomerg quoted HRT co-founder Alex Morcos as saying they had "visceral hatred" of cutthroat company cultures.
However, HRT has also made some big hires and big hires don't come cheaply. Jesse Cohen, </news/jesse-cohen-hrt> a former Goldman Sachs MD and star joined in 2018 and is thought to be running the algo development team. Xianchao Xie, a quant researcher, joined from Two Sigma in 2022 and is thought to be a big deal in the medium frequency space. In late 2025, HRT hired Harsh Padia, the chief executive of HAP Trading, to help build its options business.
Some HRT stars have also left or retired. As we were first to report, </news/oaz-nir> partner Oaz Nir quietly stepped down in 2024. Bailes Brown, an algo developer who joined from Jane Street, left in 2023 and has yet to resurface. It's not clear how much they were paid, but presumably they won't be needing to find new jobs immediately.

item.title: JPMorgan is hiring high-frequency traders for a new 'AI Markets Lab'
item.description:
JPMorgan has begun to see electronic trading firms </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-an-electronic-trading-firm> as direct competitors. Last year, it cut some of its lending to Jane Street </news/how-to-get-a-job-at-jane-street> after it made a push into credit markets </news/jpmorgan-jane-street>. In April <https://www.jpmorganchase.com/ir/annual-report/2025/ar-ceo-letters>, Jamie Dimon called Citadel Securities a "new competitor." Now, the bank is taking the fight to their turf by building a new 'AI Markets Lab' focused on high-frequency trading (HFT) and mid-frequency trading (MFT) </news/hft-jobs-medium-frequency-trading> strategies.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
The bank has hired Xi Chen, a professor at NYU, as a managing director to lead the team. He spent the bulk of his career in academia,and was named in the 2017 Forbes 30 under 30 <https://www.forbes.com/profile/xi-chen-1/> for his work on "machine learning, high-dimensional statistics and operations research." He has published multiple studies <https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=qjJg6akAAAAJ&view_op=list_works&sortby=pubdate> on dynamic pricing and also spent two years as a principal scientist at Amazon focused on the forecasting, pricing and recommendation systems of its marketplace.
AI Markets Lab sits within the bank's QTR (Quantitative Trading </news/quant-jobs-finance>and Research) group and has 12 openings across New York, London and Singapore. Job listings say the AI lab "spans signal research, pricing, market-making, execution, portfolio construction, risk management, and the production systems that support them." The bank did not respond to a request for comment regarding whether the team is (or will be) actively involved in trading, but job listings for quant researchers say that they're expected to "design, backtest, and implement market-making and risk-taking strategies." It's not clear what assets the team will be expected to trade; the Quantitative Trading and Research group as a whole trades credit, FX, equities, commodities and across "a wide range of markets."
Chen said on LinkedIn that the team is looking for more experienced people who "have been full-time in HFT or who have extensive [AI] pre-training experience." Openings for engineers request experience in low-latency C++ </news/citadel-securities-c-plus-plus-job-skills>. There's stiff competition for the kind of talent JPMorgan wants to hire; Jane Street and Citadel Securities each paid over $2m per head to their employees last year. AI labs like OpenAI have also been poking around. </news/openai-culture>
Despite the growth of electronic market-makers in the past few years, there are some areas banks still have control over. Crisil Coalition Greenwich analyst Jesse Forster said in June <https://www.greenwich.com/press-release/revenues-surging-nonbank-liquidity-providers> that "strongholds" for banks include "bespoke and structured solutions, prime brokerage, and financing products." Generally, they have control when there is minimal electronification. Efforts to increase the bank's electronic market-making capabilities could be seen as either a pre-emptive effort to keep control of those sectors should they become electronified, or a proactive strike to take back some market share from its newest rivals.

item.title: JPMorgan has a new MD in DCM, although not the usual kind
item.description:
Banking is the sell-side. You sell, right? You arrange sales, and sometimes you even go on the road and literally sell securities. Sometimes, however, your job is to buy.
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/login?_gl=1*ut8n6u*_gcl_au*MTg4MDY2NTExNi4xNzYxNTU3NDIz*_ga*ODczNzI2NTA0LjE3NTM2OTk2ODI.*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3NjM2NDM0MDYkbzI1NiRnMSR0MTc2MzY0MzQzOSRqMjckbDAkaDMyMjc4OTUzMw..>✍️
Gabe Menendez joined JPMorgan in New York this month as a managing director and head of the firm’s liability management team. He joined JPM from UBS, where he spent three years (also as head of liability management). He was part of the Credit Suisse acquisition </news/2023/12/ubs-hiring-from-credit-suisse> back in 2023 and was even head of Credit Suisse’s liability management team before being transferred to UBS. JPMorgan declined a quest to comment on this article.
Liability management is a restructuring </news/2023/05/investment-bank-restructuring>-related role within debt capital markets </news/capital-markets-jobs-ecm-and-dcm>. When a client wants to change the debt it already has outstanding, liability management professionals buy those bonds or loans back, swap them for new ones on different terms, or persuade holders to amend the existing terms. The trigger can be distress-related, but it's often just a refinancing, an acquisition, or an opportunistic move caused by a change in interest rates.
Liability management is a very in-demand role when things are not going well in the economy. It was a very fast-growing business for boutique investment banks </news/boutique-investment-banks> such as PJT back in 2024 </news/what-is-a-restructuring-banker>. Given how the economy is booming at the moment, especially in the US, Menendez might have a quiet time ahead of him in the next few months. Unless Anthropic has something to do with it <https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/anthropic-deepens-finance-push-with-10-new-ai-agents-banks-insurers-2026-05-05/>.

item.title: Citi's head of European and emerging markets sales trading is not there
item.description:
Where is Ross Taylor, the head of European and emerging markets equities trading at Citi? Not, it seems, upon the desk right now.
Citi is declining to comment on Taylor's whereabouts, but multiple sources suggest he's no longer there. We have not confirmed this with Taylor himself.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Taylor began his career over two decades ago and joined Citi from Morgan Stanley in 2021. He was promoted to head of EMEA and EM sales trading at the bank in March 2024. His FCA Registration shows him leaving at the end of July 2026, although some sources say he officially left last week.
Citi's equities sales and trading business is having a good year, with revenues up 42% year-on-year in the first half. Equities sales and trading </news/how-do-you-get-a-job-in-sales-and-trading-in-a-bank> globally at the bank is run by Fater Belbachir </news/2023/11/fater-belbachir-citi>, who is also based in London and is presumably having a good year too.

item.title: Ex-Meta manager picked up by Aristotelian hedge fund to head its engineering team
item.description:
Some time ago, Aristotle spent a few sentences discussing the meaning of “a sign”. 2,300 years later, a hedge fund </news/how-to-get-a-hedge-fund-job> named after his definition and based on magical computer sand rocks reading light signals turning money into more money has hired someone – to make the magical computer sand rocks a bit better at their jobs.
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/login?_gl=1*ut8n6u*_gcl_au*MTg4MDY2NTExNi4xNzYxNTU3NDIz*_ga*ODczNzI2NTA0LjE3NTM2OTk2ODI.*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3NjM2NDM0MDYkbzI1NiRnMSR0MTc2MzY0MzQzOSRqMjckbDAkaDMyMjc4OTUzMw..>✍️
Ziad Chammaa joined Tekmerion Capital Management in New York as head of engineering. He joined the hedge fund from Meta, where he spent just one year as an engineering manager. Before Meta, Chammaa worked at Two Sigma, where he was a VP in data engineering.
Tekmerion has had a long relationship with Brevan Howard. Originally founded in 2017, it joined Brevan’s platform back in 2024 as BH-Tekmerion. It was spun out again earlier this year. Tekmerion has three job openings currently, all in New York: one for a software engineer, one for a data analyst, and one for a macro analyst.
Tekmerion is an Ancient Greek word that means “signal”, basically. Explaining the use of the name and musing on its physical and metaphysical meaning, the firm itself said <https://www.tekmerion.fund/> that “our systematic strategies utilize sophisticated mathematical models, but at the end of the day we remain grounded in common sense and focused on achieving real, practical results.”
Tekmerion is full of eccentric figures. One of its co-founders, Zachary Squire </news/eccentric-macro-hedge-fund-manager-shows-polymaths-still-matter>, studied Classics at Princeton, before eventually becoming head of foreign exchange trading strategy and oversights at Bridgewater, where he met fellow Tekmerion co-founder Larry Mincone. It’s unclear if Chammaa speaks Greek or is particularly interested in Aristotle (he has a computer science degree), but he does have a Spanish Duolingo score of 62, for what it’s worth.

item.title: "I joined a London crypto start-up and now I am unemployed"
item.description:
I am a trading technology professional and I am unemployed through not fault of my own.
I've spent years building my career in the trading technology industry and a few years ago I had my head turned by a crypto firm. Now that firm is closing.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
My colleagues and I only learned about this situation in mid-August. We've just been given formal notice. We're all suddenly back in the job market at what seems to be a difficult moment.
We had no idea this was going to happen. Operationally, we were actually starting to see things pick up and everything seemed very positive. Suddenly everything has ground to a halt. It has been a shock.
Personally, I blame regulation. It's a bit like we were opening a huge superstore but were only being allowed to sell milk. Milk sales might be going well, but there’s only so far you can grow if you can’t put much else on the shelves.
I guess this is always a risk when you join a start-up. But if anyone's looking for good platform engineer, there are now plenty around.

item.title: A trading firm spun out of Jane Street pays £673k in London and is hiring
item.description:
Five Rings is one of the most secretive electronic trading firms </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-an-electronic-trading-firm> today. They're best known as a spinout of Jane Street, </news/how-to-get-a-job-at-jane-street> led by Ferrari driver Jason McCarthy <https://www.ferrari.com/en-EN/corse-clienti/drivers/jason-mccarthy>. Beyond that, even top trading CEOs like Alex Gerko couldn't tell you what they do. </news/difference-between-electronic-trading-firms> What we can say is that it pays handsomely, if its UK entity is anything to go off.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
'Five Rings Capital LLP' filed accounts for 2025 this week, showing that it had increased average headcount from 21 to 26. In total, it paid £17.5m ($23.6m) in 'salaries and wages', which worked out at roughly £673k ($908k) per head. This was, however, down from 2024 when it paid £806.2k per head. Some of the new arrivals in 2025 (according to LinkedIn) work in compliance, or as trading assistants, which may have brought down the average. Five Rings paid over £800k per head for three consecutive years before 2025.
The accounts suggest that Five Rings Capital didn't have the best year, as the entity had an operating loss of over £16m in 2025. Income from 'proprietary trades' nearly halved from £11m in 2024 to £6m in 2025. The entity describes its principal activities as both prop trading and "related services on behalf of the company's group," and also received £1.4m in service fees in 2025. Five Rings did not respond to a request for comment. It's possible that other entities were more profitable and that we do not have the full picture.
Despite this, Five Rings moved into a new office with space for ~60 people </news/a-quant-trading-firm-paying-806k-in-london-works-from-a-flexible-workspace> back in November, suggesting it has big plans for expansion. It's currently hiring graduate traders and software engineers as well as an experienced trading assistant.

item.title: Goldman Sachs MD says multistrategy hedge funds may yet need many more PMs
item.description:
Last year, the biggest multistrategy hedge funds </news/how-to-get-a-hedge-fund-job> hired 2,000 people. </news/multistrategy-hedge-funds-hiring>But in the past 12 months, Goldman Sachs' co-head of prime insights and analytics, says hedge fund hiring has lagged capital inflows into funds.
Speaking to the AIMA podcast, <https://www.aima.org/article/ep-142-the-long-short-the-world-according-to-goldman-sachs.html>Freddie Parker, who is also Goldman's co-head of America's capital introduction, said there have been record flows of capital into multistrategy funds over the past 12 months. Around $500bn of assets have arrived, said Parker, an increase of 25%. Flows into funds haven't been this high since 2022-2023.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
At the same time, though, Parker said that Goldman estimates that headcount grew by "more like 10-11%."
The implication is that the big multistrategy funds may need to portfolio management talent more rapidly in the second half of the year, to cope with all their new assets. Parker said large flows require "digestion" and can dull returns while funds find the talent to deploy them.
Last December, JPMorgan said <https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/hedge-funds-double-down-using-near-record-leverage-quest-boost-returns-2025-12-03/>average leverage at multistrategy funds was 645%. If this remains the case, an additional $500bn of assets implies $3.2 trillion of new leveraged assets to be managed. This, in turn, implies huge portfolio manager hiring even if existing portfolio managers scale their books.
However, Parker notes that funds are already finding ways around this conundrum by allocating money to external fund managers in ever greater amounts. Headcount at these external managers isn't measured in Goldman's figures. "Perhaps headcount growth isn't telling the full story," he admitted.
On balance, Parker said a higher rate environment is likely to be good for hedge funds. The exception will be "long-short funds that are growth-tilted," he observed.

item.title: Moelis & Co. had a great year in London, but pay did not match it
item.description:
Working at a boutique bank </news/boutique-investment-banks> like Moelis & Co. has ups and downs. For one, they can pay you wildly </news/boutique-bank-pay> when times are bad. On the other hand, however, when times turn good, you likely won’t see a moral-improving boost to your compensation.
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/login?_gl=1*ut8n6u*_gcl_au*MTg4MDY2NTExNi4xNzYxNTU3NDIz*_ga*ODczNzI2NTA0LjE3NTM2OTk2ODI.*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3NjM2NDM0MDYkbzI1NiRnMSR0MTc2MzY0MzQzOSRqMjckbDAkaDMyMjc4OTUzMw..>✍️
Moelis & Co., the boutique bank founded by Ken Moelis, recently released 2025 results for its main UK subsidiary, Moelis & Company UK LLP. The firm did very well – revenue increased by 20%, reaching £135m ($182m). It also returned to profitability after a £2.5m loss in 2024, booking a £2.6m gain.
Pay, however, did not quite match that same success. Moelis paid its London employees an average of £369k ($498k) in 2025, which was only a very slight – 4.6% – increase on 2024. In 2023, it paid an average of £375k ($505k), despite revenues that year being lower than 2025’s.
That’s partly related to hiring. Moelis has been stacking up on Londoners – it employed 256 people in the city in 2025, which was an increase on the 230 it employed in 2024 and the 211 it employed in 2023. It was the fifth year in a row that Moelis grew in London.
Moelis, as we noted previously, is a generous bank. Even when times were tough, it maintained a high compensation ratio </news/boutique-bank-pay>, meaning that it kept employee pay relatively static (and high) regardless of how the firm performed.
Moelis’ first half of 2026 results are a bit more promising than many of their peers, with revenue up by 9% and pre-tax income up by 13%. Its compensation expense, however, was up by just 3% in the same period – although its worth noting that boutique banks don’t necessarily accrue bonuses equally throughout the year.
