item.title: Morning Coffee: Barclays fixed income traders may need a lot of lasagne. HRT's boss rides the subway to work
item.description:
As we have observed here, </news/barclays-macro-to-hedge-funds> Barclays has lost quite a few macro traders to hedge funds </news/how-to-get-a-hedge-fund-job> and other banks. </news/rich-wife-banking> As we have observed here </news/adeel-khan-barclays>, Adeel Khan, head of Barclays' trading business, has been known to bond with his traders over lasagne. Now it seems that Khan may need to stock up on quantities of cheese and pasta again.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2026-09-10/barclays-traders-in-forex-options-fly-blind-when-beowulf-software-freezes?taid=6aa2e6c52d55bb00014ae66f&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_content=business&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter> reports that there are issues with some of Barclays' trading software and that when they crop up, it can cost each trader hundreds of thousands of dollars. Barclays strongly denies this, but it is worth outlining the alleged issues.
After speaking to 'half a dozen people with direct knowledge of the issues,' Bloomberg says Barclays' high-performing FX options desk and sometimes also its interest rates derivatives desk are afflicted by outages of Beowulf, a Barclays risk engine, </news/2019/09/weird-names-banks-technology-teams> that can go on for hours. During these alleged outages, traders can no longer see how the price of options would change when the underlying currency moves. When markets are volatile, this can allegedly cost each trader dearly. They are flying blind.
There have allegedly been internal complaints about this for a while, but Barclays says it is not so. A spokesperson for the bank told Bloomberg: “Stability-related incidents have fallen by more than 70% over the past four years, and we have seen no evidence linking Federal Reserve announcements to service disruptions.” The spokesperson said, too, that Barclays' traders “continue to support clients reliably across all market conditions,” and that the bank has "materially strengthened" its trading platforms.
The two things may not be mutually exclusive. It's conceivable that things are better than they used to be at Barclays, but that in the past things were very bad. Either way, it seems sufficiently frustrating that Barclays' traders have complained to a journalist. Lasagne should be deployed to placate traders until a fix is achieved.
Separately, David Solomon </news/david-solomon-goldman-sachs>, the 64-year-old CEO of Goldman Sachs, </news/how-to-get-a-job-goldman-sachs> has been known to fly to his holidays in the company jet. <https://www.businessinsider.com/david-solomon-ceo-goldman-sachs-takes-corporate-jet-2023-4>Jason Carroll, the 48-year-old co-founder and head of electronic trading </news/difference-between-electronic-trading-firms> firm Hudson River Trading (HRT), likes to ride the subway to work.
Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2026-09-10/how-jason-carroll-built-hudson-river-trading-and-a-27-billion-fortune>reports that Carroll - who appears to be worth $27bn and is the son of a coastguard rescue pilot - eschews the trappings of wealth and doesn't like luxury properties or art. He does, however, like sailing.
Carroll has an estimated 62.5% stake in HRT, but mostly likes to code. Prashant Lal, another partner, is reportedly more conspicuous internally. In this sense Carroll sounds similar to Rob Granieri </news/rob-granieri-jane-street> at Jane Street, although people at HRT do seem to know who he is.
Meanwhile...
JPMorgan was one of the primary lenders to Situational Awareness through the bank’s prime brokerage business. It cut Situational Awareness off after the losses. (FT) <https://www.ft.com/content/916eea1b-d483-49e1-9a70-53b4df8f9870?syn-25a6b1a6=1>
Situational Awareness has got ClearStreet as its prime broker now. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-11/situational-awareness-turns-to-clear-street-for-prime-brokerage?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=260911&utm_campaign=author_17940573>
Citadel made some changes to its international equities business, which will be run by 40 year old Nabeel Bhanji who joined last year from Elliott Capital Management. (FT) <https://www.ft.com/content/41fb2ff1-fb84-4ae4-8668-59d46842dcdb?syn-25a6b1a6=1>
Jane Street is the new top block trader in Asia. (FT) <https://www.ft.com/content/a2dcd05d-2bcd-40a4-adc6-cbbff016222f?syn-25a6b1a6=1>
Richard Bloomfield was an M&A lawyer working on the purchase of a maternity wear firm. He pleaded guilty to five counts of insider trading relating to the deal. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-11/ex-goodwin-m-a-lawyer-pleads-not-guilty-to-insider-trading?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=260911&utm_campaign=author_20677150>
James van Geelen, the founder of independent investment-research shop Citrini Research, has sold it to semiconductor and AI researcher SemiAnalysis. He says he's excited about this. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-11/citrini-founder-who-shook-markets-sells-firm-plans-new-fund>
A Polymarket user made $22k with bets that were all tied to companies KPMG audited. (WSJ) <https://www.wsj.com/business/c-suite/cluster-of-polymarket-accounts-won-big-on-companies-audited-by-kpmg-b4d322f7>
The UK keeps changing its tax system and only offers a four year deal on taxation of overseas wealth to new residents. “Everyone is looking at the fiscal situation and saying that these sums don’t add up. It’s the tinkering that people don’t like. Once you start tinkering, they don’t know what’s coming next.” (FT) <https://www.ft.com/content/f3ecfe7f-25df-434f-a61d-a9ce0ac1e611?syn-25a6b1a6=1>
Elan Capital Management wants a Greek office, too. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-11/dimitriou-s-elan-joins-hedge-funds-mulling-an-office-in-greece?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=260911&utm_campaign=author_19458291>
It wasn't just Chris Rokos, other Rokos Partners wanted to go to Greece as well. Chris himself was afraid of an exit tax. (Bloomberg) <https://www.thetimes.com/article/chris-rokos-tax-quit-britain-0wm0m23lq>
Greece has had a €100k flat tax rate on overseas earnings since 2019. Fund managers moving to Greece will also be charged only 5% tax on carried interest and bonuses. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-13/from-bailout-to-mayfair-rival-greece-lures-hedge-fund-elite?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=260913&utm_campaign=author_19458291>
Long-ex-Goldman Sachs trader goes viral and says that if you want to be successful you must simplify your personal life. Some people disagree. (X) <https://x.com/tradertheory/status/2098184493232447706?s=20>
"If you’re a high performer with a big personality sat among a room of mediocre people, in this environment, you’ll find yourself getting fired." (No-Rebates) <https://norebates.substack.com/p/bankers-paradise?utm_source=substack&publication_id=744072&post_id=215319815&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=qrn8&triedRedirect=true>
Goldman Sachs owns a 680,000 acre private nature reserve in Chile's Tierra del Fuego. (SpaceDaily) <https://spacedaily.com/b-goldman-sachs-came-to-own-680000-acres-of-tierra-del-fuego-when-a-timber-companys-debt-went-bad-and-instead-of-selling-the-bank-gave-all-of-it-away-to-a-wildlife-society-and-forests-once/>

item.title: Erin Piacenti's GoFundMe exceeds $1m as BofA prepares to honour her memory
item.description:
The GoFundMe <https://www.gofundme.com/f/in-memory-of-erin-piacenti-supporting-madisons-future>for Erin Piacenti </news/erin-piacenti>, the Bank of America vice president murdered on her way home in Times Square last week has reached over $1m. 9,500 people have donated, but there is still around $200k to go before the fundraiser reaches its target.
Piacenti had just returned from maternity leave. The fund is intended to help provide for her young daughter.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Many of those donating are thought to have been Piacenti's colleagues at BofA. Writing on LinkedIn, one senior member of her team said they all received the notifications of an incident on the day Erin died. "The next day, we learned that this was anything but routine," she added, saying that everyone who had the privilege of working with Erin had been "hit incredibly hard."
Bank of America is preparing to honour Erin in other ways. A spokesman for the bank said: “In accordance with Erin’s family, the bank is planning to honour her memory in a meaningful way and will share more soon.”
In an email publicizing the GoFundMe to employees, Bank of America said the GoFundMe was set up by an individual and that as such donations would not go to a registered charity. As a result, they would not be "eligible for a registered gift matching program," it explained, meaning that BofA will not match donations given.
"Thank you for continuing to support one another and for keeping Erin's family in your thoughts during this incredibly difficult time," said BofA in the email.

item.title: Jane Street, Tower & CitSec love French traders. Here's where they get them from
item.description:
Do you want a career in electronic trading </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-an-electronic-trading-firm>? Well, good for you. A top firm like Jane Street </news/jane-street-target-universities> or Citadel Securities </news/the-universities-that-will-get-you-a-300k-job-at-citadel-securities> pays its people around $2m </news/jane-street-versus-citadel-securities-pay> each on average – there’s a lot to like. The problem is, you’ll need to have an extensive background in quantitative finance </news/quant-jobs-finance>. Perhaps even a French background.
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/login?_gl=1*ut8n6u*_gcl_au*MTg4MDY2NTExNi4xNzYxNTU3NDIz*_ga*ODczNzI2NTA0LjE3NTM2OTk2ODI.*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3NjM2NDM0MDYkbzI1NiRnMSR0MTc2MzY0MzQzOSRqMjckbDAkaDMyMjc4OTUzMw..>✍️
You see, electronic trading firms love to hire French graduates. French education in mathematics is exceptional – the country has more Fields Medals than any other in the world except the USA.
But while one Grande École </news/2023/02/best-grande-ecole-finance> in mathematically-dominant France dominates Fields Medals (École normale supérieure), it is not the university that electronic trading firms, when shopping for top quantitative trading talent, go to.
Electronic trading firms run a number of internships </news/high-frequency-trading-internship>. They pay very well </news/electronic-trading-summer-internship-pay>; Optiver, for example, pays up to $10k a week to its PhD interns. Ten-week interns. $100k for an internship. Part of the price tag is that electronic trading firms are in competition with a lot of well funded rivals, such as AI companies </news/24bn-ai-lab-co-founded-by-an-ex-jane-street-intern-doesn-t-like-hiring-quants-as-much-as-open-ai>, for hiring top mathematicians.
We analysed the social media profiles of more than 250 employees, including senior staff, interns and students attending taster days at </news/high-frequency-trading-hiring-and-pay>
<https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-02/citadel-securities-seeks-millions-from-ex-staffer-who-quit-to-start-crypto-firm> </about/editor-tips>

item.title: Nomura's new global head of FX options could soon have a very wealthy wife
item.description:
Mukund Daga has spent 14 years working in FX trading. We will not opine here about the size of his bonuses, </news/bonus-increase-banking>but we will observe that there is more than one way to earn the sort of money that's commonly associated with working for the likes of Millennium. </news/how-to-get-a-job-at-hedge-fund-millennium>
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Daga, who recently left Barclays in London </news/barclays-fx-options-traders-keep-moving-on-but-hey> and who is now on his way to Nomura to be global head of FX options in Singapore, has firsthand experience of alternative ways. His wife is selling her fintech company Tazapay, which she founded six years ago with two men, for $400m. <https://investor.circle.com/news/news-details/2026/Circle-Expands-Global-Payments-Infrastructure-with-Agreement-to-Acquire-Singapore-Based-Cross-Border-Payments-Platform-Tazapay/default.aspx>
Daga didn't respond to a request to comment for this article. It's not clear how much his wife, Kanupriya Sharda, will benefit personally from the sale. Nor is clear whether he will become a househusband once her earn-out is over. Maybe they will just have a nice holiday.
Either way, six years building a B2B 'cross border payments infrastructure firm' that's sold for $400m seems like a good investment of time. Sharda was once an investment banking </news/what-is-an-investment-bank> analyst at Goldman Sachs, but she gave that up 13 years ago. Leaving banking has worked out well for her.

item.title: Popular London electronic trading head has a big new job & money to hire
item.description:
Before electronic trading firms </news/difference-between-electronic-trading-firms>were the hottest places to work, investment banks </news/what-is-an-investment-bank> gave them a pretty good run for their money. And before Credit Suisse met its sorry end, it had a pretty good electronic trading business </news/2023/08/credit-suisse-ubs-unwanted-people>. That trading business was known as AES (algorithmic execution services) and within it one man was towered above the rest. He was widely respected, widely liked and widely held to be responsible for its success: Naz Al-Khudairi. Now Naz is back, and he is seemingly in a position to hire.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
He didn't respond to a request to comment for this article, but writing on LinkedIn, Al-Khudairi said he's joined Ingenuity Trading, as chief operating officer and head of strategy. It's a trading firm that self-describes as an "AI-native, ultra-low-latency system," to improve institutional trade execution. Based in New York, it currently focuses only US equities and options. This could be about to change.
Al-Khudairi is based in London and the expectation is that his arrival will herald the opening of a new London office. It's also thought that Ingenuity will push out of US equities and into European equities, and maybe into other asset classes like FX.
The firm is in a good position to do so. In June, it raised $4.8m in seed funding <https://app.dealroom.co/news/note/ingenuity-trading-raises-4-8m-seed-to-scale-ai-native-institutional-trading> to 'expand across new products and geographies.'
In doing so, it's likely to hire. For the moment, ingenuity has around 10 full time employees, plus co-founders Pallav Chhaochhria (ex-Barclays, ex-Citi) and Karthik Teki (ex-Barclays). Chhaochhria was a former director at Barclays; Teki was a former VP. After leaving Credit Suisse in 2017, </news/2021/06/naz-al-khudairi-left-barclays> Al-Khudairi joined Barclays as global electronic trading. He left again in 2021. The two men have hired their old boss.

item.title: "The images and feelings of 9/11 remain branded on my mind."
item.description:
This is an updated version of an essay the author wrote on the 5th anniversary of 9/11.
It’s been long years since the planes came in and changed the landscape of lower Manhattan forever; long years since two commercial passenger airliners were turned into weapons of mass destruction by a small army of terrorists and flown into the North and South Towers of the World Trade Center. That attack on September 11, 2001 achieved what a truck bomb had failed to accomplish eight years earlier: the destruction of what some felt represented an architectural symbol of free market capitalism.
Anyone working in financial markets probably remembers where they were that day. I remember it as if it was yesterday. I was walking briskly across the Trade Center Plaza on my way to work when, at 8:45 a.m., I heard an explosion above my head. My first thought was that there was another bomb.
I looked up and saw a ball of fire and black smoke pouring out of a huge hole some 80 stories up the north side of the North Tower. Like most mornings, I was walking toward the bridge over West Street that connects the twin towers to the World Financial Center where I worked as a vice president of global broadcast services and president of Merrill Lynch Television.
I never made it to work that morning. And years later, the images and feelings of that day remain branded in my mind and have haunted me since. Allow me to share some of them.
Before the fall
As I gazed up at the fireball and black smoke billowing from the side of the tower, it struck me that I should probably move. Pieces of burning debris were raining down around me. I made my way toward a crowd standing under the overhang of one of the smaller trade center buildings.
It was there that I found myself standing next to a middle-aged woman sobbing silently to herself and looking up. Before I could ask her what was wrong, I followed her line of sight to the ragged hole that had been torn from the building on the 86th floor.
Standing in the flaming opening was a man in a suit. He was adjusting his tie. And then he just leaned forward and fell from the gaping inferno. He landed not far from where we were standing.
The image of the man fixing his tie, weighing his options and then deciding to face fatal impact over death by fire is as clear today as it was a decade ago.
What kind of hell was behind him in that ragged hole that convinced him that falling 86 floors and certain death was the better alternative? What could he have been thinking? "This is my final journey so I should look good"?
I needed to make sense of what I had seen, to rationalise what could have motivated him to straighten his tie to be presentable when he entered the afterlife. Basically, I was frozen in place, unable to move, until another piece of smoking debris hit a few feet away and jarred me back to reality.
I looked at my watch and saw that it was almost 9 a.m. I was going to be late for work so I started walking again towards West Street and the World Financial Center. Along the way, I stopped a policeman and asked if he knew what had caused the explosion. He said he'd heard that a small plane had accidentally hit the North Tower and ordered me to keep walking because the area was no longer safe to stand.
A low-flying jet
Because of falling debris, the North Tower was closed, so I went down to street level to cross at Vesey Street. I was making my way toward West Street, keeping my eyes on the flaming tower, mostly worried about a shift in wind and how I would deal with that. Everywhere, people were stunned, dazed, crying and in shock. I felt like I was moving through a crowd of zombies who had just had the life sucked out of them
I just kept walking, hoping to make it to the office and sanity when I saw a jet plane flying down the Hudson River. It looked like it was flying pretty low and that seemed strange. The plane flew out over New York Harbour, towards the Statue of Liberty, then banked to the left and came around...
That's when the unbelievable happened. The plane leveled off and then flew right into the South Tower of the World Trade Center, ripping through the side of the building like a chainsaw, tearing out huge chunks of glass and masonry, and sending them sailing through the air. This was no accident. Two planes meant we were under attack. I started looking for shelter, as well as for more planes.
I didn't realise it at first, but a cloud of debris knocked loose from the South Tower was coming right toward me. I screamed: "Incoming! Incoming!" The stunned people nearby looked at me like I was crazy as I urged them to move and find shelter. This was no longer a safe place to stand. I ran until I was out of breath and then looked back. Now, both towers had raging gashes in their sides and balls of fire and black smoke billowing out of them.
A world on fire
I felt like I was back in Vietnam, in a firefight, wondering from which direction the enemy would strike next. I'd had nightmares like this. But this was no dream. This was real. In all my days in Vietnam, nothing was as bad as this. This was worse than war. This was hell and the world was on fire.
I tried calling the office, but no one was picking up the phone. I figured they must have evacuated the building. There was no way to get to the World Financial Center anymore anyway. Police were moving the crowds of people out of the area. I tried to call home but there was no longer any cell phone service. I couldn't tell anyone I knew that I was still alive.
Eventually, I made my way uptown to Broadway and 66th Street, where Merrill Lynch Television had a satellite office. A television was on and everyone was watching live coverage of the attack on the twin towers. I joined them, and we watched as the South Tower collapsed, followed a few minutes later by the North Tower.
A few hours later, I reached my frantic wife by phone and told her I was okay. In the days that followed, however, I realised I really wasn't okay. Emotionally and psychologically, I was wracked with guilt and horrific images that wouldn't go away. I felt guilty that I survived while so many around me died.
A loss
My company lost three people that day. I knew one of them and went to his memorial service. He was a young man in his mid-20's who worked in our department. He was engaged to be married, with his whole life ahead of him. He was the new guy in the office.
In Vietnam, it was always "the new guy" who got it - the new guy who didn't know how dangerous the terrain was. That day the new guy didn't know he could get killed just by having breakfast in the wrong restaurant 100 floors above Manhattan.
For months following the attack, every time I closed my eyes, I could see the ball of fire over my head and the businessman straightening his tie and then his body falling to earth.
Two months after 9/11, Merrill Lynch let us return to our offices in the World Financial Center. It was way too soon. The fires from the towers were still burning. The air had the odor of death and decay. Our desks were still covered with dust, and there were particles in the air. As I sat in my chair, I had the feeling I was surrounded by ghosts.
It's been 10 years since I last walked across the Trade Center Plaza, past the giant metal globe glistening in the middle of a water fountain, where children would play and tourists would stop and take pictures. The plaza isn't there anymore. For many years, there was just a giant hole reminding us of the innocent and brave lives that were erased that day. It was like an open wound that wouldn't heal; a hole in the heart of a city in mourning.
Today, a new modern skyscraper is being erected in its place to both memorialise the spirits of nearly 2,700 souls who reside there and to show the world that life and commerce goes on, in a free-market world, even an economically challenged one.
Fred Yager was an embedded war correspondent in Vietnam working as a US Navy journalist. He’s also a former writer for the Associated Press, CBS News and Fox Television. On September 11, 2001, Fred was director of Global Broadcast Services and president of Merrill Lynch Television. He’s also a former editor of eFinancialCareers in North America.

item.title: Morning Coffee: HSBC says goodbye to its biggest cost cutter. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley bankers have a tricky choice of chatbot
item.description:
Success is, according to a general consensus of bankers, considerably better than failure. But there is one slight caveat to be made, which is that there is sometimes a terrible kind of finality to it. If a project fails, then (as long as management and shareholders will allow it), you can keep on struggling. If it succeeds, then there will be a time when the project is over, no more, and then you have to decide what you are going to do next.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Something like this thought might have been on the mind of Pam Kaur <https://www.ft.com/content/63e733d1-2c0f-46c5-ae6b-de1a72d4e9df?syn-25a6b1a6=1>, who has decided that after two years as CFO of HSBC, it is “the right time in my career to embrace new leadership opportunities and apply my experience in a different context”. She was appointed to the job by Georges Elhedery, </news/georges-elhedery-hsbc> as one of his first actions on being promoted to CEO, and has been present for the major restructuring </news/hscb-closure-europe-us-job-cuts> that Elhedery put in place, including significant redundancies. </news/hsbc-ai-job-cuts>
And you don’t win a battle like that without taking some psychic casualties. In fairness to Elhedery, he has very much taken ownership of the decision, and Kaur was apparently not even in the top three most feared managers </news/hsbc-s-self-proclaimed-ruthless-ceo-is-not-its-most-feared-person> at HSBC. But nevertheless, when costs are being cut, it is the finance department which has the responsibility of agreeing the budgets, and usually the CFO who needs to be present at all the fractious budget meetings. It must have been a stressful couple of years, and one which might have been likely to leave anyone thinking that a change of scene and a new challenge would be welcome. Possibly including a new set of colleagues who don’t remember the conflicts of the past, although Kaur is apparently going to remain in an advisory post on “ongoing strategic projects” for a while.
It’s interesting to note that Pam Kaur may have learned the skills of personal resilience that served her so well at HSBC in a previous job which, perhaps surprisingly, seems to have been quite the crucible of champions. She joined the HSBC group in 2013 to be head of internal audit, coming from Deutsche Bank. The other famous alumnus of the Deutsche internal audit division is, of course, Christian Sewing, who managed to implement a similarly successful turnaround. Perhaps the lesson is that if someone has seen and survived the all of the things that were present at Deutsche in the early 2010s, there is nothing left in banking that could possibly scare them.
Elsewhere, OpenAI has launched “ChatGPT for finance <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-10/openai-debuts-chatgpt-for-financial-services-an-investment-banker-tool>”, a tuned version of its flagship Astra model which has built-in access to data from a number of vendors and is meant to either replace junior bankers, or to help them more efficiently generate models and presentations. According to Nick Turley, VP of Product, “We’re effectively teaching ChatGPT to research like an analyst and back up its conclusions like an analyst”.
Turley is not an investment banker </news/what-is-an-investment-bank>, so it’s possible that he wasn’t being sarcastic when he said “like an analyst”. But this does potentially raise a bit of a problem for some bankers, because OpenAI’s product launch is meant to directly compete with a similar set of plugins <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-02-24/anthropic-links-ai-agent-with-tools-for-investment-banking-hr> for Anthropic’s Claude chatbot.
Famously, tech bankers like to ostentatiously use </news/2019/08/michael-grimes-morgan-stanley> their clients’ products. This includes AI agents – the bankers on the SpaceX IPO had to spend a while <https://www.nytimes.com/2026/04/03/business/spacex-ipo-grok-elon-musk.html> trying to work with Grok. But Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are sharing the lead role on the forthcoming IPOs of both OpenAI and Anthropic. So whose chatbot should they use?
For the bankers actually working on the deals, it’s an easy decision – use the one that is relevant to your team. But what about everyone else? There are already some difficult internal politics to negotiate </news/goldman-sachs-morgan-stanley-openai-anthropic>, with everyone at both banks keen to demonstrate that both tech companies are being treated fairly and that information separation is maintained. If one chatbot catches on, then the bankers for the other team might reasonably feel like they’re being snubbed. So wise junior bankers might feel like it’s best to have two robot friends rather than one for a while.
Meanwhile …
The Chinese government has decided to tell bankers how to do their jobs. With the local IPO calendar as crowded as a rush-hour underground train, representatives from the securities regulator have apparently been speaking to bankers, warning them that they only want to see flotations of quality companies and national champions, and that they would prefer a “conservative” approach to pricing, so that the Shanghai market gets a reputation for stocks that go up rather than down. (FT <https://www.ft.com/content/012b9a34-445d-483c-a6c6-1fbd52e60731?syn-25a6b1a6=1>)
Hannes Hofmann is going from JPMorgan to HSBC to be their global head of family offices. He will be joined by his colleague, Cayman Wills, who quite possibly has the most appropriate name possible for an ultra-high net worth banker. (Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-09/jpmorgan-veteran-hofmann-joins-hsbc-in-global-family-office-push>)
Christopher Woolcott has pleaded guilty to four counts of fraud after inventing a number of fake identities and filing forged documents in order to make it look like there was a takeover bid for a Canadian oil exploration company. (FT <https://www.ft.com/content/d3fe6f10-d03e-4580-b033-1fd39f9f8f97?syn-25a6b1a6=1>)
There are still Partners at Goldman Sachs, but there are only seven “Partner partners”, who were members of the partnership before it became a limited company in 1999. Now there will be six, as Sharmin Mossavar-Rahmani, CIO of the global wealth management business, is retiring. (Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-10/goldman-s-exclusive-club-shrinks-again-with-sharmin-mossavar-rahmani-s-exit?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=260910&utm_campaign=author_21835441>)
“Selling the family silver” used to be the ultimate expression of disgrace, but lots of people these days would actually much rather have a decent cash inheritance than a load of old fashioned cutlery that can’t go in the dishwasher. (WSJ <https://www.wsj.com/lifestyle/kids-dont-want-family-silver-melt-it-down-86026f42?st=Q2qi7W&reflink=desktopwebshare_permalink>)
A global luxury brand has to get very angry before it does this; the Dorchester Hotel has got tired of a member of the Qatari royal family not paying a bill, and has applied to a court for an order to let it sell the car he parked there. It was only a £25,000 Abarth compared to a bill of nearly half a million, but it’s the principle of the thing presumably. (FT <https://www.ft.com/content/031b8b28-8a95-499f-b3f4-216d3b3b70df?syn-25a6b1a6=1>)

item.title: Hedge fund QRT interviewed heavily for its discretionary macro team. Now it's made a decision
item.description:
Qube Research and Technologies </news/qrt-hedge-fund> (QRT) has been diversifying. When it spun out of Credit Suisse in 2018, it was focused on systematic equities. <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2017-08-01/credit-suisse-is-said-to-spin-out-a-1-billion-quant-hedge-fund>Since then, it's moved into fundamental equities under Stephen Irvine </news/qube-research-hires-ex-balyansy-hedge-fund-founder-who-closed-fund-last-year>, commodities under Naveen Arora, and catastrophe bonds under Raphael Rayees.
Now it's also diversifying into discretionary macro trading, and has made a significant hire.
Qube declined to comment for this article, but we understand from multiple sources that a head of discretionary macro trading has been appointed and will join soon. Thereafter, he or she is expected to build a team.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Macro portfolio managers say Qube was interviewing heavily for the role and that various people got the call. The identity of the successful individual remains unclear. If you know, please clarify it immediately using the contact details at the bottom of this article.
Qube is very French. It is also very unorthodox. People who have worked there in the past told us they have limited visibility on personal PnL and that portfolio managers don't run individual books. Instead, they are expected to provide trading strategies that are coded into Qube's systems and then receive allocations of money from Qube's central fund depending upon performance. The people providing strategies aren't always aware how much their strategy was allocated, or how it performed. Sometimes one strategy is combined with another, further obscuring things.
For portfolio managers used to receive a percentage of personal PnL as compensation, this be unnerving. Bonuses are discretionary and up to 75% must be invested </news/qube-qrt-pay> in Qube's own funds for a period of years.
This approach has enabled Qube to keep compensation costs low and to keep hiring. When it spun out of Credit Suisse in 2018, Qube employed 100 people. Now it employs well over 2,000 </news/hedge-fund-qube-research-and-technologies-appears-to-be-trimming-a-few-people> people and is adding more.
Most of Qube's hires are technologists or quants, though. Macro portfolio managers are rarer sorts of beasts. Not all macro PMs will be attracted by Qube's set-up. But someone has been.

item.title: Barclays has a new MD, with a curious past
item.description:
In recent years, AI has come for everyone, threatening to upend the financial order. In previous epochs, however, it was tokenisation that was coming for everyone, threatening to upend the financial order. AI experts are having a field day. It turns out that tokenisation experts are having a good time these days, too.
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/login?_gl=1*ut8n6u*_gcl_au*MTg4MDY2NTExNi4xNzYxNTU3NDIz*_ga*ODczNzI2NTA0LjE3NTM2OTk2ODI.*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3NjM2NDM0MDYkbzI1NiRnMSR0MTc2MzY0MzQzOSRqMjckbDAkaDMyMjc4OTUzMw..>✍️
Artem Korenyuk joined Barclays this month as head of digital asset strategy, based in New York. He joined the British bank from Citi, where he spent three years, and was most recently head of the bank’s enterprise digital assets team. He was also a managing director (MD) at Citi.
Korenyuk joined Citi in 2026 as something of a homecoming; he started his career with the firm, back when he was in operations. He left the firm and spent 11 years at The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC), an industry-owned cooperative belonging to the banks using it that settles US securities. Neither Korenyuk nor Barclays responded to a request for comment.
As we’ve touched on before </news/ai-in-operations>, tokenisation (which is what digital assets are – tokenised assets) is a huge threat to traditional banking operations </news/operations-jobs-banking>. That’s because tokenising assets renders vast swathes of a bank’s workforce null, especially in the age of AI.

item.title: Spring internships have become harder to get, and less useful too
item.description:
Spring internships </news/spring-week-bank> have been, for some time, the best way to start your career in finance in the UK. Get in the pipeline nice and early, convert it into a summer internship </news/internship-investment-bank>, convert that into a job. Things might be changing, however.
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/login?_gl=1*ut8n6u*_gcl_au*MTg4MDY2NTExNi4xNzYxNTU3NDIz*_ga*ODczNzI2NTA0LjE3NTM2OTk2ODI.*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3NjM2NDM0MDYkbzI1NiRnMSR0MTc2MzY0MzQzOSRqMjckbDAkaDMyMjc4OTUzMw..>✍️
New data from Trackr <https://the-trackr.com/>, formerly the Bristol Tracker, said that 2026 spring internships were significantly more difficult to get than 2025 ones – and led to fewer summer internships, to boot.
In 2026, the average aspiring spring intern applied to 35 different roles. That was comparable to their 2025 colleagues, who applied to 33, on average. However, just 51% of applicants in 2026 received some sort of offer, compared to 74% of their peers in 2025.
The other downside for 2026 applicants was that spring internships became less useful. 31% of spring interns received return offers in 2025, but in 2026, it was just 20%. Instead of concrete offers, banks increased the number of students being fast-tracked for interviews next year. They also increased the number of outright rejections.
What’s driving the changes? A few things. For one, although spring internships are aimed at first-year students, fewer first-year students were getting into them, with more places instead going to third-year students, Trackr noted. 2% of spring interns were third-year students, Trackr said in 2025, and that number increased to 5% in 2026. The number of second-year students was flat across both years at 24%, suggesting that first-year students suffered on account of their third-year peers.
This might be bad, this might be good. America doesn’t really have spring internships anymore (not since the diversity apocalypse the other year </news/bank-diversity-programs>), and the student recruitment process there seems to be doing just fine. And bank internships have become more difficult to get </news/bank-acceptance-rate> over the last few years, too. The situation is becoming worse everywhere – have no fear that you are in an exclusively bad situation.

item.title: Hamza Lemssouguer's Arini Capital Management is doing more than ok
item.description:
Aged 29, Hamza Lemssouguer was the darling of London's credit trading industry. Working on Credit Suisse's high yield desk, he reportedly </news/2021/07/credit-suisse-top-traders-leaving> made $120m in a single year. Aged 35, Lemssouguer is possibly having less of a good time: he runs his own $20bn credit hedge fund Arini Capital Management, and Arini was reportedly down 8% in July and another 1% in August.
Both the Financial Times <https://www.ft.com/content/a62199d1-9388-4735-a4f0-db519c84eb79?syn-25a6b1a6=1> and Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-20/lemssouguer-s-hedge-fund-loses-8-in-july-on-soured-credit-bets> have raked over Lemssouguer's woes, which are reportedly the result of soured bets on the likes of Aston Martin and Altice International.
Lemssouguer didn't respond to a request to comment for this article. But sources say Arini Capital Management is performing better than the recent coverage suggests. Over four years of existence, it's understood to have delivered net returns of 73%, with a Sharpe of around 1.3. The S&P 500 returned around 52% over the same period.
Arini has also been hiring. At its last set of accounts, filed for the year ending December 2024, Arini employed fewer than 50 people. Now it has 180, up 25% in 12 months. While other hedge funds churn through their staff, Arini is understood to have a high retention rate. Fewer than 10% of Arini's investment team members have left in the past five years, including both firings and voluntary departures. That's abnormally low.
This isn't to say that no one has left. Gavin Yates, the CEO of Arini in the US, is said to be going to Citadel to be a credit portfolio manager. Ben Elliot left in London, too.
Nor is to say that times aren't tough - Arini owns hundreds of millions of pounds worth of Aston Martin's debt, and the value of that debt has plummeted following a controversial refinancing deal. <https://www.investorschronicle.co.uk/content/bc457795-73de-4e8a-a03e-29afbe3d05c5?srsltid=AfmBOorXL3MeJgk8e9OiOx-IjuQCMj1WziODh43Cbw-Si787MFJKLM_h>
Distressed debt investing can be a long game, though. Arini has been down before. In 2022, it lost 15% over a few months. In 2024, it lost 8% over two months. Then it gained 29% over the next 12 months. Patience.

item.title: Standard Chartered hired an ex-Credit Suisse trader for its e-trading team in Singapore
item.description:
Alex Manakyan was at Mizuho, but not for long. After joining Mizuho's Singapore office as head of FX trading in October 2024, he left again in September 2025. He was presumed retired and happily managing his own money.
Not any more.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
After a year out of the market, Manakyan is making a comeback. He will soon join Standard Chartered as global co-head of automated risk management (ARM) trading.
This sounds like a more substantial role than the one he was last engaged in, so maybe Manakyan was lured by the prospect of more responsibility.
Alternatively, he may have been lured by the prospect of working with Simon Wilson <https://www.risk.net/people/7963563/people-stanchart%E2%80%99s-new-risk-chief-citi-hires-for-fx-and-more>who also used to work for Credit Suisse and who was hired by Standard Chartered in May as global head of automated risk.
Wilson will reportedly be focusing on digitising FX and rates trading platforms and applying AI across the markets business. Manakyan will presumably be focused on trading across the same broad spectrum.
The Singapore Monetary Authority Register says that Ben Connolly, the former head of e-trading for Standard Chartered in Asia and Europe, left the bank's Singapore team in late August.
Connolly spent 15 years at Standard Chartered.
Manakyan's arrival may shake things up.

item.title: Two Sigma raised pay in London last year but some people left
item.description:
Two Sigma is looking to grow its London team in 2026; the hedge fund </news/biggest-quant-hedge-funds> moved into a new office with double the floor space </news/two-sigma-new-office-london>and room for up to 200 people. Accounts for 2025 filed via the UK's Companies House </news/best-paying-hedge-funds> over the past week suggest it has to fill a few extra seats if it wants to pack that office out.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Headcount across both of Two Sigma's entities fell last year. 'Two Sigma International Limited,' its hedge fund entity, fell from 93 people to 85 through losses in both its modelling and engineering teams. 'Two Sigma Securities UK Limited,' the fund's market making arm, fell from 14 employees to 13 after one trader departed.
Spending on 'salaries and wages' was up in both entities. The hedge fund paid £502.8k ($681.5k) per head, while the market making arm paid £535.9k ($726.3k).
When Two Sigma first moved to its new office in Devonshire Square, it occupied one floor (roughly the same sized office as it previously occupied) and began refurbishing the floor above for them to occupy later. Estates Gazette <https://www.estatesgazette.co.uk/news/two-sigma-and-pfa-take-18500-sq-ft-at-devonshire-square/> said yesterday that it has officially leased that second floor and could be ready to unleash its hiring plans. At present, though, it only has one opening in operations and two in reliability engineering.
Squabbles atop Two Sigma's leadership team may also be a reason the fund has yet to push the button on hiring. Last month, Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-27/two-sigma-s-feuding-founders-head-to-arbitration-in-fresh-battle>reported that the fund sent a letter to investors notifying them that founders John Overdeck </news/hedge-fund-divorce> and David Siegel are going into another round of arbitration. The pair have had a public feud over the past few years that led to them resigning as co-CEOs in 2024.

item.title: Morning Coffee: JPMorgan's 29-year-old female MD is having a fine career. Real life big spending dilemmas
item.description:
Angie Long seems like an illustrious sort of person. Equipped with an economics degree from Princeton and a history of female rugby-playing, Long made managing director (MD) and was promoted to run JPMorgan's high yield credit trading desk aged only 29. She has a CFA Charter. She developed the concept <https://txwsw.com/angie-knighton-long-cfa/> of the high yield debt index. Now she's about to sell a $37bn collateralised loan obligation (CLO) platform first funded by some Pizza Hut moguls. <https://txwsw.com/angie-knighton-long-cfa/>
How do you get to become like Angie? It's worth noting that she made MD aged 29 at JPMorgan in 2004; these days most of the new young trading MDs seem to be men. </news/newly-promoted-29-year-old-goldman-sachs-md-escapes-to-hedge-fund-millennium>Angie had a great mentor in the form of Blythe Masters, female inventor of the credit default swap. She has a great husband, Chris, who also went to Princeton, who also worked for JPMorgan, and also founded the $37bn CLO platform, which Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-09/husband-and-wife-plan-sale-of-37-billion-credit-firm-palmer-square?taid=6aa17ca9d5b7470001dffd6f&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_content=business&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter> reports the Longs - married for 25 years - are now about to sell.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
It could have been very different. In 2007, the Financial Times <https://www.ft.com/content/31814002-c680-11db-be1a-000b5df10621> reported that Angie had considered resigning from JPMorgan a year after her daughter was born. Working and motherhood were too hard, said the FT. But JPMorgan wanted to keep Angie Long and so let her take a leave of absence and then come back to work for 20 hours a week in a specially created role working out of Kansas City.
“I dealt with some creative people in human resources who told me to think outside of the box. I didn’t have to choose a full-time or a standard role,” Angie Long declared at the time. It was a sign of how far women's rights had come, declared the FT in 2006. It was also a sign of how good Angie was and how hard it was to find people. “When you have someone as strong as Angie, you work hard to find the right seat for them,” declared her male JPM boss. “Competition for talent is at all-time highs...so you have to be creative about talent retention.”
20 years later, Angie has four grown-up children and is about to sell Palmer Square Capital Management, the $37bn CLO platform she founded with Chris in 2009 in the tiny place of Mission Woods, Kansas <https://www.missionwoods-ks.org/>. Bloomberg notes that the two have been riding the quadrupling of the CLO market ever since and that Palmer Square is one of the largest CLO issuers, despite being based in Kansas. Investors like the recurrent fees that CLOs generate. Angie is having a fine career; it might not be so easy for women now.
Separately, people working in AI Labs in Silicon Valley are holding Iliad-themed naked wrestling parties and trying to make generational money in the five years before AGI renders humanity extinct. <https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/anthropic-researcher-quits-over-out-of-control-ai-fears-707b7628>
When they do make this money, the WSJ <https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/ai-tech-anthropic-openai-ipo-0a9da59e?utm_source=bluesky,threads,twitter>says many of the AI guys and AI women don't know what to do with it. One moment they were earning $300k salaries. Now they've sold stock and have $30m+.
The most popular purchase in these situations seems to be an espresso machine. This might be supplemented by a sauna. Maybe a watch. Someone bought a $35k vase.
Meanwhile...
5,000 new people went to work in Abu Dhabi's financial hub in the first half of this year. There are now 49,000 people there in total. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-08/abu-dhabi-finance-hub-draws-4-700-new-professionals-despite-war?taid=6a9ff9f0298afe0001c62b05&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_content=business&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter>
Hedge fund Millennium is opening in Athens. Hedge fund Verition wants to. The Greek finance minister is coming to London to talk to other hedge funds. The UK allows 100% tax relief on foreign earnings for four years; Greece allows it for 15 years. “For highly mobile wealthy individuals, the decision is increasingly about the overall package: tax certainty, lifestyle, connectivity and access to Europe.” (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-09/millennium-joining-rokos-with-plans-for-first-greek-outpost?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=260909&utm_campaign=author_19458291>
Hamza Lemssouguer's Arini Capital Management lost 8% in July and nearly 1% in August. Blame its investments in Aston Martin and Altice International. Arini is doubling down on conviction trades and some are pointing out that it lost 8% over two months in early 2024, then gained about 29% over the following 12 months. (Financial Times) <https://www.ft.com/content/a62199d1-9388-4735-a4f0-db519c84eb79?syn-25a6b1a6=1>
US Treasury secretary Scott Bessent is saying things like "I have asymmetric information", and "I am the house now," and, "You can be against me if you want," as he buys Japanese yen. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-08/bessent-dares-traders-to-bet-against-yen-i-am-the-house-now?taid=6aa094a0f4ee7b0001a49a39&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_content=business&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter>
The Treasury department said on Wednesday that it would buy back $6bn in US government debt in the first buyback operation since Bessent in mid-August announced the expanded programme. (FT) <https://www.ft.com/content/2476992f-c9fe-4992-887d-f34c81c100ab?syn-25a6b1a6=1>
Scott Bessent made his name 30 years ago, betting against sterling while working with George Soros. “The Treasury Secretary’s ‘put’ should be taken seriously,” says a strategist at Citi. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-09/traders-brush-aside-scott-bessent-s-bet-against-me-tough-talk?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=260909&utm_campaign=author_21122136>
Jefferies hired Joram Siegel to build an outsourced fixed income trading platform in 2024. Now it's changed its mind and is firing him and closing the platform. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-09/jefferies-to-wind-down-outsourced-fixed-income-trading-business?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=260909&utm_campaign=author_21061455>
IG Group, the London-listed online trading platform, is cutting hundreds of jobs. (Sky) <https://news.sky.com/story/online-trading-platform-ig-group-takes-axe-to-hundreds-of-jobs-13583591>
A 22-year-old posed as a representative of Gemini crypto exchange and Google and conned $245m of bitcoin from a man in Washington. Then he bought a fleet of sports cars, rented mansions in Miami and spent $569k in a single night at a club. (Yahoo) <https://uk.news.yahoo.com/22-old-pleads-guilty-alleged-021441698.html>

item.title: How to get an H1B visa for a banking job: the data
item.description:
Changes to the H1B visa </news/trump-h1b-visa-change-salary-finance> system may be on the horizon, but it's still a massive funnel of talent </news/h1b-visa-investment-banking-jos> into investment banks. Big US banks employ thousands of H1B visa holders </news/h1b-visa-pay-banking>, and some profiles are more common than others. We've looked at over 17,500 salary listings on the H1B visa salary database over the last two years (ending July 31st 2026) to see what kinds of roles banks are most likely to result in banks wanting to sponsor you for a H1B.
This is how you'll get an H1B for banking now.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
1. Work in technology (or maybe the front office)
Across the five biggest US banks, just under half of all H1B filings are confirmed to be for engineers or other technology staff. The next most common function (separated by a huge margin) is front office staff, including bankers, traders and relationship managers. Front office H1Bs are also the highest earning; they make $180k salaries on average but many earn $300k or more. </news/the-300k-h1-b-visa-jobs-that-banks-forsake-us-staff-for>
Other functions that are popular for H1Bs are quants, risk and compliance staff. Roughly 20% of filings didn't declare any function and simply stated seniority.
2. Be a VP (or an engineering lead)
It's the mid-level staff, particularly vice presidents, who benefit most from the H1B visa scheme. 38% of H1B visa-holders in banking are vice presidents, earning an average salary of $171k. Associates follow closely behind with 25% of the total share of H1Bs.
Where seniority (in the traditional banking sense) is not specified, the most common job titles are senior engineers and lead engineers, which equate to roughly the same seniority as associates and VPs.
If you're a managing director and need to move to the US, banks will usually rely on something like an L1 visa which involves working in another office abroad before joining in America, or an O-1a visa reserved for people with "extraordinary ability." </news/0-1a-visa-quant-trading-h1b>MDs represent just 0.4% of the H1B pool, but they at least give an indication of how much you can earn if you make MD yourself: average salaries across H1B MDs is $407.4k.
3. Work in New York
Unsurprisingly, the most popular destination for H1Bs is New York. It accounts for 28.5% of all H1B hires (37% if you include Jersey City) and pays an average of $176k. There are some cities where you'll be paid more.
Working in technology for a bank in California can be lucrative. The US banks pay salaries of $182k on average in San Francisco and $198k in Palo Alto. Sadly, these hires make up just ~2% of the total talent pool.
Pay in 'Y'all Street' is much lower. Banks have tech hubs across multiple cities in Texas, including Dallas, Irving and Plano; average salaries for H1Bs in these cities are all below $156k. H1Bs in Dallas earn just $127k on average.
4. Earn $160k (unless you work at Goldman Sachs </news/h1b-visa-changes-goldman-sachs>)
Average pay across the five biggest US banks was $154k. Most banks paid more than this but one paid considerably less.
Goldman Sachs, the second biggest employer of H1Bs, paid an average of just $136k across 3969 filings. All the other US banks (bar Wells Fargo) paid above $160k on average with Morgan Stanley paying the most: $165.5k
Of course, if you've yet to obtain an H1B you're likely earning much less than this. Bloomberg reported last November <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2025-11-11/trump-s-h-1b-visa-curbs-banks-to-add-more-finance-specialist-jobs-in-india#:~:text=For%20most%20roles,with%20the%20matter.> that a $60k salary for a visa holder in the US could get the same quality of candidate as a 300k rupee ($3.4k) salary in India (where most H1B visa-holders originate). This suggests most H1B visa nominees are paid around 860k rupees ($9k).
Goldman's numbers might be bogged down by the fact that it hires a large number of analysts on H1Bs, many of whom work outside its New York base. The median salary for Goldman is $128k, which suggests there are some particulary high earners bringing up the average.
Things might change from next year onwards. A weighted lottery is being introduced that splits H1B nominees into 4 brackets based on their wages; those in the highest bracket get four entries into the H1B lottery while the lowest tier candidates get just one. More MDs on $400k may soon be making their way to New York.

item.title: If you can find some good data, hedge funds will hire you
item.description:
In March, we said that data strategists </news/hedge-funds-and-market-makers-need-data-strategists-as-war-heats-up>were hot. It's September and this is still so.
Tudor Investment Corporation has just hired a new data strategist in London. He is Conor Taggart and he will seemingly be Tudor's data strategy lead.
Tudor declined to comment. Taggart did not read our message. He appears to have arrived at Tudor recently.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Data strategists source, evaluate, clean and render into usable formats, data that might be used for hedge funds to generate alpha. Good data is very valuable. Good data strategists are in demand.
Before he worked for Tudor, Taggart worked for Eagle Alpha. Before he worked for Eagle Alpha, he worked for Millennium. </news/how-to-get-a-job-at-hedge-fund-millennium>
Various other data strategists have also swapped jobs this year. Dan Ostermueller arrived at Jane Street in July after previously working for Citadel. Kevin Chiu arrived at Tower Research in August, after previously working for BlackRock. Adam Brown arrived at Jump Trading, also in August, after previously working for Morgan Stanley. Rokos hired Meredith Brown in New York as a macro data strategist in July.
Quants can work in data strategy too. In Citadel's large data strategy team, for example, there are quant researchers who describe <https://www.citadel.com/careers/career-perspectives/real-people-real-impact-how-alternative-data-powers-investment-decisions-at-citadel/?utm_source=li&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=dsg>their function as, turning "noisy data into outputs that are intuitive, timely and directly usable."

item.title: Banking HireVue interviews: what they are, what they’ll ask you for 2027
item.description:
If you’re angling for a 2027 banking and financial services internship </news/internship-investment-bank>, you might very well have a HireVue interview </news/2022/10/hirevue-interview-banking> coming up.
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/login?_gl=1*ut8n6u*_gcl_au*MTg4MDY2NTExNi4xNzYxNTU3NDIz*_ga*ODczNzI2NTA0LjE3NTM2OTk2ODI.*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3NjM2NDM0MDYkbzI1NiRnMSR0MTc2MzY0MzQzOSRqMjckbDAkaDMyMjc4OTUzMw..>✍️
What are HireVue interviews exactly? These days, they’re just interviews. Weird, creepy interviews, but still interviews. A pre-recorded message from HR (or an AI-generated HR bot) will play, your microphone and camera will be tested, and you’ll be prompted to answer some questions.
Answer them as though a human had asked them, don’t worry about your ums and your ahs, and hope for the best. It’s very straightforward. AI will not count your nose follicle density. AI will not count your blinks to assess your fear response. AI will transcribe and assess your answer, however. The sort of questions you’re asked are behavioural questions </news/70-top-banking-interview-questions-and-how-to-answer-them>, also known as “fit” questions. These are the kinds of questions that lend themselves to the STAR technique </news/finance/the-s-t-a-r-interview-technique>.
If your answers are good, you’ll be given the thumbs up by the machine and your case will now be handled by a human being in an applicant tracking system. Congratulations, breath out, you’re onto the next step.
You will have a limited period of time to answer the questions, depending on who is interviewing you. We have a list of standard response times by firm here </news/how-long-to-answer-hirevue-interview>. They typically vary from 30 seconds of prep and 90 seconds to answer (for Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley) to a whopping 180 seconds of prep and 90 seconds to answer (for BlackRock).
The questions below come from a variety of sources, including (but not limited to) Glassdoor, WallStreetOasis, and Reddit. They’re mostly, but not exclusively, questions asked of interns, mostly in America and the UK. And they’re all, as far as we can tell, questions that have been asked this recruiting season.
Generic questions
Tell me about yourself. Walk me through your resume/CV. Why this bank? Why investment banking? Why this division? Which team are you most interested in? What are your strengths and weaknesses? Where do you see yourself in five years? How do you keep up with the markets? What are you following at the moment?
Goldman Sachs
If you accidentally sent an email containing confidential information to a client, how would you first respond? How would you maintain client confidentiality between a manager and a client? Why [this department], specifically, for the long term? Why [this city]? What's a book, article or paper you recently read? How do you identify and assess the key risks in a new project or investment? Talk about a recent event that impacted financial markets. Tell me about a time you made a process more efficient. Describe a time you had to work with a difficult team member.
JPMorgan
Tell us about a recent piece of news that you read about that affects the business division you are applying to. What motivates you? Tell me about a time when you were challenged to be persistent to reach an important goal. What obstacles did you face? How did you overcome them? Tell me about a time when you produced an innovative strategy for a unique problem. Describe the situation, your actions, and the outcome of the situation. Tell me about a time when you did the right thing, even when it was difficult. How do you handle information and break it down? When was a time you showed humility? Talk about a time you solved a business problem and got a result.
Morgan Stanley
What was the biggest failure in your life? Tell me about your leadership experience and what you learned from it. Tell me about a time you did the right thing. Tell me about a time you worked on a team project that you struggled with. Tell me about a time you worked in a group. Why [city]?
Citi
How would you describe investment banking to someone who doesn't know anything about finance? How does a bank make money? How does an interest rate change impact bank revenue? How do recent global or economic news events impact the bank? How do you think about personal banking products? What is a recent tech trend that Citi should employ? When was a time that you put a lot of time and effort into something and it did not work out? What did you learn from it?
Bank of America
Why you are interested in this programme and/or business? Describe two trends happening in your chosen department/field. Which one of your key accomplishments best illustrates your personal initiative and willingness to push beyond what is required? Name a time you juggled multiple tasks and how you managed your time. Tell me one instance where you solved a problem proactively. Tell me about a time you struggled. Tell me a time when you collaborated with others or demonstrated leadership. How do you work in a multicultural and multigenerational team?
Barclays
What has happened in markets this past year? Do you have a portfolio? What's in it? Explain one of the projects mentioned on your resume in detail, including your role, the technologies used, the challenges you faced, and how you solved them. Tell me about a time you faced a risk. Tell us about a time you displayed initiative.
Deutsche Bank
How are banks doing right now in historical terms? What news article interested you the most recently? Describe a teamworking situation. When did you encounter a conflict? What is a skill you have that is not on your CV? Would you rather work in teams or independently? How would you act if you had the opportunity to participate in a project you had no experience with? Would you take on the project, or stick to projects you already know how to do?
UBS
Tell me one M&A deal you are following recently. What do you think [of it]? Apart from F1, what is a different sport that UBS should sponsor? If you could choose to sponsor one sport globally, which sport would you choose, and why? How does this role contribute to the whole company? Why work in New York specifically? What is the most interesting thing you know? Describe a time you had to do something new. How do you lead a team?

item.title: Goodbye to the London digital assets trading venue that hired 62 people
item.description:
Times change, things move on. In May 2025, GFO-X launched <https://www.thetradenews.com/gfo-x-launches-regulated-trading-venue-for-centrally-cleared-assets/> an "FCA regulated trading venue for centrally cleared assets." On September 3rd 2026, GFO-X posted on its website <https://www.gfo-x.com/notices.html>that it was ceasing its activities with immediate effect.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
No one seems to have noticed GFO-X's move, except may its 62+ employees who presumably are already or will be soon out of jobs.
A spokesperson for GFO-X said, ""After careful consideration, GFO-X Group has taken the decision to wind down its UK business and suspend trading on its UK venue."
He also said: "GFO-X was established with a clear strategic vision: to create a trusted, regulated institutional venue for digital asset derivatives. The UK business achieved notable milestones, including regulatory approvals, clearing arrangements, participant onboarding and significant trading activity (£3bn traded notional)." But, “Market conditions and strategic considerations have evolved since launch."
GFO-X was founded by Arnab Sen, the former founder of Harbour Capital Management, and Rajesh Melwani, the chief operating officer of Harbour Capital Management. The two worked together in Hong Kong.
Although it terminated itself last Friday, GFO-X made various upbeat posts on LinkedIn recently. One said it was "delighted" to add prediction markets activities in Dubai. Another said it was reaching milestones and praised the "team for tenacious drive to keep delivering."
Insiders say it's only the London office that's currently affected. GFO-X's website says it's still hiring interns and compliance and tech staff. Applicants may need to be more tenacious than ever.

item.title: "I ran a team full of talented banking MDs. I had to fire them as they wouldn't leave"
item.description:
I have spent decades working in banking. I ran a significant business for a significant US bank. I am not divulging my true identity here.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
It is not uncommon for this website to write about managing directors (MDs) being let go by investment banks. These people are often vocal and disgruntled. They complain and it makes a good story.
I want to explain what it's like from the other side.
The team I ran cut a lot of MDs. They were talented, established managing directors but there were too many of them. We were no longer a pyramid-shaped hierarchy.
These MDs would not move on. The market we cover has become smaller and opportunities to change jobs are fewer. In the past, there would be fluidity of movement and rotation between banks, but this has stopped and people have become entrenched.
In management, it is necessary to deal with this. A strong manager encourages people to move on, or creates new roles for them to move into.
In my team, I encouraged the entrenched MDs to leave but it made no difference. They wouldn't go. They were preventing some very talented vice presidents (VPs) and directors from growing into jobs with more responsibility.
Eventually, I had no choice. I had to rebalance the pyramid to allow our strong junior talent to move up. It was a tough decision and we lost some really good people. I don't regret it, though. Without them, the juniors are thriving.
Steven Gilmore is a pseudonym

item.title: Starling Bank's Anne Boden wants to compete with Anthropic for talent at new AI fintech
item.description:
It has been over three years </news/2023/05/anne-boden-tom-blomfield-starling-bank-monzo>since Anne Boden stepped down as CEO of Starling Bank </news/starling-bank-tempers-its-back-to-office-push-for-hybrid-engineers>, the digital banking unicorn most recently valued at £4bn ($5.4bn). After an extended period of absence, she now looks to be back in the startup game and has some lofty hiring aspirations.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Boden said in a LinkedIn post earlier today that she's hiring for a "MoonShot" project and wants to hire people who are deciding between "making your fortune at Anthropic, or launching your own AI start-up." Boden describes the new venture as "engineering led" and "well paid with equity."
It's another fintech </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-fintech>, rather than a new AI lab. Boden said that the company will be "right at the start of the next revolution in banking technology," and ideally wants people with three years of banking tech experience. Speaking at a conference in June, <https://www.linkedin.com/posts/anneboden_starling-activity-7468412867655008256-Izzu?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop&rcm=ACoAADRgqxoBNsXkSGtQtgsWn7LCW2KwTIyI2g0> Boden said that banks will be "opening bank accounts to agents" rather than individuals, and that app-based banks will be a thing of the past. Her new project may have something to do with that.
Boden has been working on AI quietly since 2023, when she renamed one of her companies 'AI by Boden.' In micro-accounts for 2025 released on Companies House, the entity had just 3 employees. She did not respond to a request for comment on whether this new initative will be an expansion of that entity or whether it will be a new, standalone project.
Starling Bank has been pushing heavily into AI as well, launching an agentic money manager in March. It has also used AI to cut jobs; The Guardian <https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/jul/03/starling-bank-cuts-130-jobs-boosts-ai-investment>reported in July that the bank was cutting 130 roles, but Starling said it was "continuing to hire tech and AI engineers."

item.title: The £50k course that may, or may not, get you a £90k banking job in the UK
item.description:
Doing a master’s in finance </news/the-top-30-masters-in-finance-for-getting-a-job-in-investment-banking> can be great for your career, yes, but there is an alternative, rather less known and generally more popular in Europe – the master’s in management (MiM). In many ways the baby brother of the MBA </news/best-mba-for-finance-banking>, and much like the MBA, not all MiMs were created equal.
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/login?_gl=1*ut8n6u*_gcl_au*MTg4MDY2NTExNi4xNzYxNTU3NDIz*_ga*ODczNzI2NTA0LjE3NTM2OTk2ODI.*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3NjM2NDM0MDYkbzI1NiRnMSR0MTc2MzY0MzQzOSRqMjckbDAkaDMyMjc4OTUzMw..>✍️
The most authoritative source of MiM worthiness, the Financial Times’ rankings <https://rankings.ft.com/rankings/3047/masters-in-management-2026>, found that – for the 16th year in the last 17 – the Swiss University of St. Gallen offered the best MiM in the world. Swiss universities in general provide excellent MiMs.
British universities do not, however. Since 2018, when the FT’s ranking expanded to 100 universities (from 65), UK universities have consistently underperformed on the ranking, being either the worst or second worst on average among major countries (which we’ve defined as France, Germany Italy, Spain, Switzerland, and the UK).
Part of that problem is that British MiM courses struggle with employability. The FT has measured employability after three months of graduation since 2019. In that year, British universities were on top of their peer group – 96% of students had a job after three months. In 2026, just 79% did, the lowest of their peer group.
A university like </news/the-top-100-universities-globally-for-careers-in-banking-and-finance> London Business School (LBS) is a good example of the decline. LBS’s MiM graduates had an employment rate of 94% after three years in 2019. In 2024, this employment rate declined to 91%. In 2025, to 90%. In 2026, to 88%.
The MiM employment rate at Warwick Business School, one of the UK’s traditional target schools </news/target-universities-finance-uk> for financiers, has declined even more dramatically. In 2019, 98% of Warwick MiM graduates were employed three months after graduation. In 2026, 82% were.
The University of Edinburgh’s business school is even worse. From a 3-month employment rate of 95% in 2019, it's now down to 66%.
All of these MiMs cost money, and a pretty pile of it, too. LBS’ MiM cost <https://www.london.edu/masters-degrees/masters-in-management/fees-financing-and-scholarships> £53k. Warwick’s cost <https://www.wbs.ac.uk/courses/masters/management/fees/> £42k. Even Edinburgh, where a third of students didn’t have a job after three months of graduation, cost £35k.
If you do get a job, it could be lucrative. The FT says LBS MiM graduates make an average of $120k (£89k) in 2026. At an 88% success rate, that might be worth a punt. Warwick’s graduates make an average of $74k (£55k). Edinburgh’s graduates make an average of $71k (£52k). At what point is it no longer worth that punt?
Maybe better to do a master’s in finance </news/the-top-30-masters-in-finance-for-getting-a-job-in-investment-banking>. Or even a master’s in financial engineering </news/top-masters-in-financial-engineering-courses>.

item.title: Citi hired a top BofA saleswoman in London and is moving her to Asia
item.description:
It's not always the case that people want to leave London for Asia. Witness Greg Guyett, </news/2022/10/greg-guyett-hsbc> who didn't want to go at HSBC and who managed to hang on for a bit </news/greg-guyett>in London instead. If you have family in Asia, though, maybe it's a bit easier.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Sophia Wang is making the trip. Wang, who has an MBA from London Business School, has been in London since 2010 according to the FCA Register. She spent most of that time at Bank of America, where she was latterly an MD in global fixed income and commodity sales. Now Wang is taking her attributes to Citi.
The FCA Register shows Wang leaving BofA in April 2026. Multiple sources say she is joining Citi in Asia with a focus on North Asian sales. Citi has not confirmed this and did not respond to requests to comment for this article. Yang did not respond either.
Citi has been building out its Asian fixed income business. Last year it hired Christoher Chan from Goldman Sachs as head of Asia north and South Markets solutions. In November, it hired multiple new FX salespeople. <https://www.thetradenews.com/citi-expands-fx-team-in-japan-asia-north-australia-and-asia-south-with-seven-new-hires/>Wang is a major hire. Citi's existing North Asia sales team includes the likes of Chen Ni, head of FX institutional sales and Davy Tsang, head of rates investor sales.
